<skill_content name="brainstorming">
# Skill: brainstorming

# Brainstorming

You are very good at building. You build what you believe your human
partner wants, and that belief is usually thinner than it feels. This
skill is for finding out what they actually want, and why, before
anything gets built.

People often haven't finished working out what they want. Good questions
help them think it through. When you understand the why, you make the
hundred decisions they never mention the way they would have made them.

## First: What Do You Actually Know?

Before you reply, ask yourself: what do I know about what they want, and
why?

- **Everything that matters is in the request** ("make the icon cornflower
  blue"). This is a quick, clear task. Do it, and say what you did.
- **Something non-trivial is missing.** Start the conversation.

## Your First Message

Your first message is two things, in this order:

1. One line letting them know that if they'd rather skip the questions and
   have you just start, they can say so. If they take you up on it, this
   skill is done: state any significant how-it-gets-made choice
   (platform, language, medium) in one plain line, then do what they
   asked through the normal workflow.
2. One open question that gets them describing. Ask about a real moment
   or a concrete picture: "What's the moment you find yourself wishing
   this existed?" or "Tell me about the people who'll be in the room."

That's the whole message.

## The Conversation

Each message ends with one question: a single sentence with no list of
example answers hanging off it. Use plain language, pitched just a little
above where your human partner is. Match their vocabulary; never use
process jargon.

Be clear and concise. Lead with what matters. Avoid jargon. When you
report what you found, give them the most important findings and offer
the rest.

**Get them describing.** Open questions come first. Their own words carry
intent that your options can't. Offer a short menu only when they're
stuck. When they say "just guess" or "what do you think?", propose
something concrete.

**How it gets made.** Every project rests on choices about medium, tools,
materials, and resources: the platform, programming language, and
libraries for an app; the medium for a piece of art. Find out early which
of those choices they want to make, which they're handing to you, and what
they already have to work with. Someone with strong views or skills will
want to talk it through. Someone counting on you needs sensible defaults,
said in plain words. When there's existing work, build on what it already
uses. Any choice you make goes in the design as your call, never as
something they agreed to.

**Ground to cover.** This is territory, not a script. Never read these
out as questions:

- what kind of thing this is, and what makes it special
- why now, and what success looks like to them
- goals, non-goals, and anti-goals (what would make this a failure even
  if it technically works)
- prior art: what they've seen elsewhere, loved or hated
- current state: what exists now, what they've tried
- the details they care about

**Questions that work** anchor in specifics: "Walk me through the last
time...", "If it could only do one of these well, which?", "What would
make you wince if I got it wrong?" A guess they can correct ("I'm
guessing this is because X keeps biting you?") often beats a question.

**Offer recon.** Once you have a bit of grounding and looking would help,
offer to go look: their codebase or project, their own files and data,
or the web. Say what you'd look for. They decide whether you go.

**Think wide privately.** Before you propose anything, come up with
several ideas and drop the weak ones, including any that fight what
they've told you about why. Show the comparison only when it helps them
decide.

**Show, don't tell.** Offer the visual companion (below) whenever seeing
would help more than reading:

- something they'll look at: a screen, a page, a printout, a sign
- a layout or arrangement: of a screen, a room, a schedule
- a flow or a sequence of steps
- options that would look different from each other
- a structure that's easier to see than read: a diagram, a timeline, a map

Once they've accepted, use it for mockups to react to, side-by-side
options, and throwaway prototypes they can click.

**Spike to feel things out.** Agentic work is waterfall, but very, very
fast. A quick throwaway build is often the cheapest way to learn what
they want or whether something works. Offer one when it would help.
When they just want to spike, get out of the way. Spikes get no tests
or minimal ones, aren't bulletproof, and skip the plan, implementation,
and review process. Bring what the spike taught you back into the
conversation.

## Play It Back

Play back as you go. As soon as you understand one part well enough to
describe it (what it's for and who it serves, say, or how one piece
behaves), describe that part back in about 200-300 words, then return to
questions about the next part. Playback and questions alternate through
the whole conversation; the last chunk covers whatever is left.

Mark anything you're guessing as your guess; only what they said goes in
as theirs. End each chunk by asking what's wrong or missing.

Before you send a chunk, check it: does it describe something they'll
look at, like a page, a screen, a schedule, or a printout? If so, and
they haven't seen the visual companion offer yet, send the offer instead
(its own message, below) and hold the chunk for the next message. Once
they've accepted, put a mockup next to the description.

## Size the Work

Once you understand what they want, pick a size and say it in plain
words. They can override it.

| Size | The full description | Then |
|------|----------------------|------|
| A quick, clear task | the request itself | do it |
| A small change | in chat | build it through the normal workflow |
| A project with a written design | a written design document | a full plan (for software: superpowers:writing-plans) |

If it grows mid-task, stop, say so, and step up a size.

If this is really several independent projects, say so, agree on an
order, and brainstorm them one at a time.

## The Written Design

For a project, write a plain document a talented builder in the domain
could plan from without going back to your human partner. Cover:

- intent and the why
- goals, non-goals, anti-goals
- constraints
- the parts of the how they decided, as they decided them
- what's left to the builder

**Where it goes:** in a software repo,
`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, committed.
Otherwise, ask. Your human partner's preferences override both.

**Builder check:** dispatch a fresh subagent with
`builder-check-prompt.md` in this directory. When you tell your human
partner you're writing it up, say a reviewer will read it first and you
may come back once with a few questions. Don't hand over the document
until the check is back. Sort what the builder asks into three piles:

- **Answered already** by the conversation or the project: put the answer
  in the document.
- **Minor:** a sensible builder could settle it without changing what gets
  built. Settle it yourself and mark it in the document as your call.
- **Theirs:** only your human partner can answer it, and the answer changes
  what gets built.

Bring the "theirs" pile in one message, most important first. Update the
document with their answers, then hand it over with a short list of the
calls you made so they can check those while reading. That's the only
round of questions the check produces. Without a subagent tool, read the
document as that builder yourself.

<HARD-GATE>
Nothing gets built until your human partner approves the full
description: in chat for a small change, the document for a project.
Building includes writing product code, scaffolding, installing
dependencies, creating projects, and invoking an implementation skill.
Reading and exploring are fine.

Two exceptions. If they opted out of the questions, the skill is done
and the gate goes with it. A spike they said yes to may be built; it
stays labeled throwaway, and keeping what it produced is a new request
that comes back through this gate.

After a project's document is approved, the next step is the plan. For
software, invoke superpowers:writing-plans and no other skill.
</HARD-GATE>

## Red Flags

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "I'll offer options to save them effort" | Options steer. Ask them to describe it first. |
| "I'll fill in sensible defaults" | Good. Say them out loud. A default they never heard is one they couldn't reject. |
| "I should explain the process first" | Ask your question. The process shows itself. |
| "They said 'sounds good' to the idea" | Approval covers what you showed them. A description you haven't written isn't approved. |
| "The spike works, I'll keep building on it" | Keeping it is a new request. Back through the gate. |

## Visual Companion

A browser tab for showing mockups, diagrams, and prototypes. It's a
tool, not a mode: accepting it doesn't send every question to the
browser.

**Offer it just-in-time.** Offer it the first time one of the moments
above comes up, never upfront. The offer is its own message with nothing
else in it:

> "This might be easier if I show you. Want me to open a browser tab with some mockups?"

If they decline, stay in text and don't offer again unless they raise it.

**Per question, ask: would they understand this better by seeing it?**
Mockups, layouts, diagrams, and side-by-side designs go in the browser.
Requirements, scope, tradeoffs, and conceptual choices stay in text. A
question about a UI topic isn't automatically a visual question.

If they accept, read `visual-companion.md` in this directory before
starting the server.

1: """Error types for Agentic ODI operations.
2: 
3: Every failure mode in the domain has a dedicated exception class so callers
4: can branch on the *kind* of failure instead of matching on message text. All
5: ODI errors inherit from :class:`OdiError`, so a single ``except OdiError``
6: catches anything this package raises deliberately.
7: 
8: Note that :class:`ValidationError` here is the *ODI contract* error. Pydantic's
9: own ``ValidationError`` remains available from ``pydantic`` and is unrelated.
10: """
11: 
12: from __future__ import annotations
13: 
14: 
15: class OdiError(Exception):
16:     """Base class for every deliberate Agentic ODI failure."""
17: 
18: 
19: class ValidationError(OdiError, ValueError):
20:     """Input did not satisfy the ODI contract.
21: 
22:     Also a :class:`ValueError` so that callers written against the previous
23:     behaviour (which raised bare ``ValueError``) keep working unchanged.
24:     """
25: 
26: 
27: class NotFoundError(OdiError):
28:     """A referenced resource does not exist.
29: 
30:     ``hint`` is an optional sentence telling the caller what to do next. It is
31:     appended to the message so it survives into user-facing output.
32:     """
33: 
34:     def __init__(self, resource_id: str, kind: str, hint: str | None = None) -> None:
35:         self.resource_id = resource_id
36:         self.kind = kind
37:         self.hint = hint or ""
38:         message = f"{kind} not found: {resource_id}"
39:         if self.hint:
40:             message = f"{message}. {self.hint}"
41:         super().__init__(message)
42: 
43: 
44: class ConflictError(OdiError):
45:     """The requested change conflicts with the current state."""
46: 
47: 
48: class RateLimitError(OdiError):
49:     """The caller exceeded an allowed rate or volume."""
50: 
51:     def __init__(
52:         self, message: str = "Rate limit exceeded", retry_after: float | None = None
53:     ) -> None:
54:         self.retry_after = retry_after
55:         super().__init__(message)
56: 
57: 
58: class ConsentRequired(OdiError):
59:     """The agent tried to act on the workspace before the PM agreed to it."""
60: 
61: 
62: class StoreError(OdiError):
63:     """The persistence layer could not complete the operation."""
64: 
65: 
66: class SerializationError(OdiError):
67:     """A payload could not be converted to or from its wire format."""
68: 
69: 
70: _STATUS_BY_ERROR: tuple[tuple[type[OdiError], int], ...] = (
71:     (ValidationError, 400),
72:     (NotFoundError, 404),
73:     (ConflictError, 409),
74:     (RateLimitError, 429),
75:     (ConsentRequired, 403),
76:     (StoreError, 500),
77:     (SerializationError, 502),
78: )
79: 
80: 
81: def error_status(err: OdiError) -> int:
82:     """Map an ODI error onto the HTTP status code that best describes it.
83: 
84:     Unknown :class:`OdiError` subclasses fall back to ``500`` rather than
85:     raising, so a new error type can never break an error handler.
86:     """
87:     for error_type, status in _STATUS_BY_ERROR:
88:         if isinstance(err, error_type):
89:             return status
90:     return 500

2: 
3: from __future__ import annotations
4: 
5: from enum import Enum
6: from typing import Any
7: 
8: from pydantic import BaseModel
9: 
10: 
11: class StudioErrorCode(str, Enum):
12:     MCP_UNREACHABLE = "mcp_unreachable"
13:     MCP_TOOL_FAILED = "mcp_tool_failed"
14:     LLM_UNREACHABLE = "llm_unreachable"
15:     LLM_TOOL_ROUNDS_EXHAUSTED = "llm_tool_rounds_exhausted"
16:     NOT_FOUND = "not_found"
17:     VALIDATION = "validation"
18:     OUT_OF_RANGE = "out_of_range"
19:     CONFLICT = "conflict"
20:     INTERNAL = "internal"
21: 
22: 
23: class StudioError(BaseModel):
24:     code: StudioErrorCode
25:     message: str
26:     detail: str | None = None
27:     suggestion: str | None = None
28:     retryable: bool = False
29:     request_id: str | None = None
30: 
31: 
32: _OUT_OF_RANGE_MARKERS = (
33:     "must be between",
34:     "out of range",
35:     "must be greater than",
36:     "must be less than",
37: )
38: _VALIDATION_MARKERS = (
39:     "is required",
40:     "must not be empty",
41:     "invalid ",
42: )
43: 
44: 
45: def parse_tool_result(text: str) -> StudioError | None:
46:     """Return a classified error for an MCP error string, or ``None`` on success."""
47:     if not text:
48:         return None
49: 
50:     stripped = text.strip()
51:     lowered = stripped.lower()
52:     is_error = lowered.startswith("error:") or " not found:" in lowered
53:     if not is_error:
54:         return None
55: 
56:     message = stripped
57:     if lowered.startswith("error:"):
58:         message = stripped[len("error:") :].strip()
59: 
60:     lowered_message = message.lower()
61:     if "not found" in lowered_message:
62:         return StudioError(
63:             code=StudioErrorCode.NOT_FOUND,
64:             message=message,
65:             suggestion="Check the identifier and try again.",
66:         )
67:     if "unreachable" in lowered_message or "connection refused" in lowered_message:
68:         return StudioError(
69:             code=StudioErrorCode.MCP_UNREACHABLE,
70:             message=message,
71:             suggestion="Check that the MCP server is running, then retry.",
72:             retryable=True,
73:         )
74:     if any(marker in lowered_message for marker in _OUT_OF_RANGE_MARKERS):
75:         return StudioError(
76:             code=StudioErrorCode.OUT_OF_RANGE,
77:             message=message,
78:             suggestion="Use a value inside the documented range.",
79:         )
80:     if any(marker in lowered_message for marker in _VALIDATION_MARKERS):
81:         return StudioError(code=StudioErrorCode.VALIDATION, message=message)
82: 
83:     return StudioError(code=StudioErrorCode.MCP_TOOL_FAILED, message=message)
84:

92:     if content:
93:         first = content[0]
94:         text = getattr(first, "text", None)
95:         if text is not None:
96:             return str(text)

1: # Data Flow
2: 
3: ## Sources of Truth
4: 
5: | Layer | Owns | Persists |
6: |---|---|---|
7: | `packages/core` | `Job`, `Step`, `Outcome`, `CustomerOutcome`, `ODIService`, repository protocol | SQLite event log + snapshots |
8: | `apps/mcp-server` | MCP tool adapters over `ODIService` | `build_repository()` selects SQLite in production and in-memory for `AGENTIC_ODI_DB=:memory:` |
9: | `apps/studio-api` | Studio API, canvas projection, chat tool loop, conversation history, PM memory | Via the same repository when the local backend is active; conversations and memory in `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db` |
10: | `apps/studio` | Presentation state, optimistic canvas updates | Browser cache only |
11: | `apps/cli` | Terminal rendering, local/remote backend selection | SQLite directly for `local`, no local writes for `mcp` |
12: 
13: ## Write Paths
14: 
15: ### Local CLI
16: 
17: ```text
18: agentic-odi customer-outcomes add
19:   -> LocalBackend
20:   -> ODIService
21:   -> SQLiteRepository
22:   -> IntentStore (append) + snapshot refresh
23: ```
24: 
25: ### MCP
26: 
27: ```text
28: MCP client / Studio MCP mode / CLI --backend mcp
29:   -> FastMCP tool
30:   -> ODIService
31:   -> configured Repository
32: ```
33: 
34: `apps/mcp-server` builds its repository once at import time with `build_repository()`. Production uses SQLite; tests set `AGENTIC_ODI_DB=:memory:` (the root test suite does this in `tests/conftest.py`).
35: 
36: ### Studio API
37: 
38: ```text
39: apps/studio SPA
40:   -> /api/canvas, /api/steps, /api/outcomes
41:   -> backend=local: ODIService -> Repository
42:   -> backend=mcp:   call_mcp_tool -> MCP server -> ODIService -> Repository
43: 
44: apps/studio SPA
45:   -> /api/chat
46:   -> stream_chat -> OpenAI-compatible LLM -> MCP tool calls
47:   -> StudioMemory (conversation turns + remembered observations)
48: ```
49: 
50: The studio memory is a separate SQLite file, not an ODI repository. It never
51: feeds the canvas; it only supplies bounded context to the next chat turn.
52: 
53: The SPA sends `mcp_url` with every data request for compatibility. In `local` mode the sidecar ignores it; in `mcp` mode it is required for canvas and mutations.
54: 
55: ## Read Paths
56: 
57: ```text
58: ODIService.get_jobs / get_job_map / get_outcomes
59:   -> Repository read-through state
60:   -> Pydantic models
61:   -> JSON (CLI --json, MCP text payload, Studio canvas)
62: ```
63: 
64: The Studio canvas falls back to the demo seed only in `mcp` mode when MCP is unreachable or returns no jobs. `local` mode returns exactly what is in the local database, including an empty canvas.
65: 
66: ## Configuration
67: 
68: | Variable | Used by | Default |
69: |---|---|---|
70: | `AGENTIC_ODI_DB` | core SQLite repository | `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db` |
71: | `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND` | CLI, Studio API | `local` |
72: | `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | CLI, Studio defaults | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` |
73: | `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DB` | Studio API memory | `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db` |
74: | `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DIST` | Studio API, dev launcher | `apps/studio/dist` |
75: | `AGENTIC_ODI_REPO_ROOT` | Tauri shell | auto-detected |
76: | `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` | CLI chat, Studio chat | `http://localhost:8001/v1` |
77: | `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` | CLI chat, Studio chat | `local-tools-model` |
78: | `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` | CLI chat, Studio chat | `local` |
79: 
80: ## Trust Boundaries
81: 
82: - The SPA runs in a browser or Tauri webview and only trusts the sidecar origin.
83: - The sidecar may reach MCP and the LLM; CORS is restricted to known Studio origins.
84: - MCP is an HTTP service with no authentication in local development. Do not expose it directly to the internet; the Cloudflare setup tunnels the sidecar, not MCP.
85: 
86: ## The Failure Path
87: 
88: A failure is a first-class result, not an empty success. The path is the same
89: for the CLI, the sidecar, and the SPA.
90: 
91: ```text
92: MCP tool result (text)
93:   -> agentic_odi_core.remote.parse_tool_result
94:   -> StudioError { code, message, detail, suggestion, retryable, request_id }
95:   -> sidecar: StudioHTTPError -> HTTP status + {"error": StudioError}
96:   -> SPA: StudioApiError -> FailurePanel (message, detail, suggestion, Retry)
97: ```
98: 
99: - **One error body.** Every HTTP failure is `{"error": StudioError}`. The SPA
100:   also reads a legacy `{"detail": "..."}` body, so an older sidecar still
101:   produces a readable message. Write routes no longer wrap their result in
102:   `{"ok": true, "result": ...}`: a success is the object, a delete is
103:   `{"deleted": id}`.
104: - **One terminal chat event.** Every `/api/chat` stream ends with exactly one
105:   `message` or one `error`. A recoverable tool error stays a tool result the
106:   model can read, but it is reported as `status: "error"` and counted. A fatal
107:   failure ends the stream with `event: error` carrying the `StudioError`.
108: - **Request ids.** The sidecar accepts or mints `X-Request-ID`, echoes it on
109:   the response, and puts it on every SSE frame. The MCP server's own log line
110:   and the `Execution` record (#82) do not carry it yet, and authentication
111:   (#90) is out of scope.
112: - **The canvas is a union.** `CanvasState` is `loading | ready | empty |
113:   error`. An empty canvas is an invitation; a failed canvas is a failure panel
114:   with Retry. The two never look the same.
115: - **The turn log is safe.** One JSON line per turn carries the request id, the
116:   model, the round and tool counts, the error count, the duration, and the
117:   outcome. Sensitive keys are dropped rather than redacted, so no token, key,
118:   or customer quote can reach the log.

1: """HTTP error shape, status mapping, and request-id handling for the sidecar.
2: 
3: Every failure the Studio API reports travels as one body::
4: 
5:     {"error": {"code": ..., "message": ..., "detail": ..., "suggestion": ...,
6:                "retryable": ..., "request_id": ...}}
7: 
8: The model itself lives in :mod:`agentic_odi_core.remote` so the CLI and the
9: sidecar agree on what a failure is; this module owns the HTTP mapping.
10: """
11: 
12: from __future__ import annotations
13: 
14: import logging
15: import re
16: from typing import Any
17: from uuid import uuid4
18: 
19: from agentic_odi_core.remote import StudioError, StudioErrorCode
20: from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
21: from fastapi.exceptions import RequestValidationError
22: from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
23: from starlette.datastructures import Headers, MutableHeaders
24: from starlette.exceptions import HTTPException as StarletteHTTPException
25: from starlette.types import ASGIApp, Message, Receive, Scope, Send
26: 
27: logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
28: 
29: REQUEST_ID_HEADER = "X-Request-ID"
30: 
31: #: A request id is echoed in responses and written to logs, so it must be a
32: #: short, boring token. Anything else is replaced with a fresh one.
33: REQUEST_ID_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$")
34: 
35: STATUS_FOR_CODE: dict[StudioErrorCode, int] = {
36:     StudioErrorCode.NOT_FOUND: 404,
37:     StudioErrorCode.VALIDATION: 422,
38:     StudioErrorCode.OUT_OF_RANGE: 422,
39:     StudioErrorCode.CONFLICT: 409,
40:     StudioErrorCode.MCP_UNREACHABLE: 502,
41:     StudioErrorCode.LLM_UNREACHABLE: 502,
42:     StudioErrorCode.MCP_TOOL_FAILED: 500,
43:     StudioErrorCode.LLM_TOOL_ROUNDS_EXHAUSTED: 500,
44:     StudioErrorCode.INTERNAL: 500,
45: }
46: 
47: CODE_FOR_STATUS: dict[int, StudioErrorCode] = {
48:     400: StudioErrorCode.VALIDATION,
49:     404: StudioErrorCode.NOT_FOUND,
50:     409: StudioErrorCode.CONFLICT,
51:     422: StudioErrorCode.VALIDATION,
52:     500: StudioErrorCode.INTERNAL,
53:     502: StudioErrorCode.MCP_UNREACHABLE,
54: }
55: 
56: 
57: class StudioHTTPError(Exception):
58:     """A failure that already knows its HTTP status and its error model."""
59: 
60:     def __init__(self, error: StudioError, status_code: int | None = None) -> None:
61:         self.error = error
62:         self.status_code = status_code if status_code is not None else status_for_code(error.code)
63:         super().__init__(error.message)
64: 
65: 
66: def status_for_code(code: StudioErrorCode) -> int:
67:     """Return the HTTP status that belongs to an error code."""
68:     return STATUS_FOR_CODE.get(code, 500)
69: 
70: 
71: def code_for_status(status_code: int) -> StudioErrorCode:
72:     """Return the error code that belongs to an HTTP status."""
73:     return CODE_FOR_STATUS.get(status_code, StudioErrorCode.INTERNAL)
74: 
75: 
76: def request_id_for(request: Request) -> str:
77:     """Return the request id assigned to this request, or an empty string."""
78:     return str(getattr(request.state, "request_id", "") or "")
79: 
80: 
81: def _error_body(request: Request, error: StudioError) -> dict[str, Any]:
82:     request_id = request_id_for(request)
83:     if not error.request_id:
84:         error = error.model_copy(update={"request_id": request_id})
85:     return {"error": error.model_dump(mode="json")}
86: 
87: 
88: def _error_response(request: Request, error: StudioError, status_code: int) -> JSONResponse:
89:     request_id = request_id_for(request)
90:     headers = {REQUEST_ID_HEADER: request_id} if request_id else None
91:     return JSONResponse(_error_body(request, error), status_code=status_code, headers=headers)
92: 
93: 
94: def studio_error_handler(request: Request, exc: StudioHTTPError) -> JSONResponse:
95:     """Render a :class:`StudioHTTPError` as the one error body."""
96:     return _error_response(request, exc.error, exc.status_code)
97: 
98: 
99: def validation_error_handler(request: Request, exc: RequestValidationError) -> JSONResponse:
100:     """Render a request-body validation failure as a ``validation`` error."""
101:     detail = _compact_validation_text(exc)
102:     error = StudioError(
103:         code=StudioErrorCode.VALIDATION,
104:         message="Request validation failed.",
105:         detail=detail,
106:         suggestion="Check the request body and try again.",
107:     )
108:     return _error_response(request, error, 422)
109: 
110: 
111: def _compact_validation_text(exc: RequestValidationError) -> str:
112:     parts: list[str] = []
113:     for error in exc.errors():
114:         location = ".".join(str(part) for part in error.get("loc", ()))
115:         parts.append(f"{location}: {error.get('msg', 'invalid')}")
116:     return "; ".join(parts)
117: 
118: 
119: def http_error_handler(request: Request, exc: StarletteHTTPException) -> JSONResponse:
120:     """Render a Starlette/FastAPI ``HTTPException`` as the one error body."""
121:     error = StudioError(
122:         code=code_for_status(exc.status_code),
123:         message=str(exc.detail),
124:     )
125:     return _error_response(request, error, exc.status_code)
126: 
127: 
128: def unhandled_error_handler(request: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:
129:     """Log an unexpected failure and return it without internals."""
130:     request_id = request_id_for(request)
131:     logger.exception("unhandled studio-api error (request_id=%s)", request_id, exc_info=exc)
132:     error = StudioError(
133:         code=StudioErrorCode.INTERNAL,
134:         message="Something went wrong. The team has been notified.",
135:     )
136:     return _error_response(request, error, 500)
137: 
138: 
139: def _safe_request_id(candidate: str | None) -> str:
140:     """Return the client's request id when it is safe to echo, else a fresh one."""
141:     if candidate and REQUEST_ID_PATTERN.match(candidate):
142:         return candidate
143:     return uuid4().hex
144: 
145: 
146: class RequestIdMiddleware:
147:     """Accept or mint an ``X-Request-ID`` and echo it on the response."""
148: 
149:     def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp) -> None:
150:         self.app = app
151: 
152:     async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
153:         if scope["type"] != "http":
154:             await self.app(scope, receive, send)
155:             return
156: 
157:         request_id = _safe_request_id(Headers(scope=scope).get(REQUEST_ID_HEADER))
158:         scope.setdefault("state", {})["request_id"] = request_id
159: 
160:         async def send_with_request_id(message: Message) -> None:
161:             if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
162:                 MutableHeaders(scope=message)[REQUEST_ID_HEADER] = request_id
163:             await send(message)
164: 
165:         await self.app(scope, receive, send_with_request_id)
166: 
167: 
168: def register_error_handlers(app: FastAPI) -> None:
169:     """Install the one-error-body handlers on an app."""
170:     handler: Any = studio_error_handler
171:     app.add_exception_handler(StudioHTTPError, handler)
172:     handler = validation_error_handler
173:     app.add_exception_handler(RequestValidationError, handler)
174:     handler = http_error_handler
175:     app.add_exception_handler(StarletteHTTPException, handler)
176:     handler = unhandled_error_handler
177:     app.add_exception_handler(Exception, handler)

13: from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware

17: from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.connectors import ConnectorService
18: from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.errors import (

27: CORS_ORIGINS = [

39: def default_spa_dist() -> Path:
40:     """Resolve the built SPA, preferring an explicit override."""
41:     configured = os.environ.get("AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DIST")
42:     if configured:
43:         return Path(configured)
44:     return Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4] / "apps" / "studio" / "dist"

47: SPA_DIST = default_spa_dist()

49: 
50: def create_app(
51:     repo: Repository | None = None,
52:     backend: str | None = None,
53:     connectors: ConnectorService | None = None,
54:     memory: StudioMemory | None = None,
55: ) -> FastAPI:
56:     if repo is None:
57:         repo = SQLiteRepository()
58:     service = ODIService(repo)
59:     app = FastAPI(title="Agentic ODI Studio API")
60:     app.state.service = service
61:     app.state.backend = backend or os.environ.get("AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND") or DEFAULT_BACKEND
62:     app.state.connectors = connectors or ConnectorService()
63:     app.state.memory = memory or StudioMemory()
64: 
65:     app.add_middleware(
66:         CORSMiddleware,
67:         allow_origins=CORS_ORIGINS,
68:         allow_credentials=False,
69:         allow_methods=["*"],
70:         allow_headers=["*"],
71:     )
72:     app.add_middleware(RequestIdMiddleware)
73:     register_error_handlers(app)
74: 
75:     @app.get("/health")

77:         return {"status": "ok"}
78: 
79:     @app.get("/capabilities")
80:     def capabilities() -> dict:
81:         return {"capabilities": app.state.backend}
82: 
83:     app.include_router(studio_router)
84: 
85:     if SPA_DIST.is_dir() and not os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_DISABLE_SPA"):
86:         assets_dir = SPA_DIST / "assets"
87:         if assets_dir.is_dir():
88:             app.mount("/assets", StaticFiles(directory=assets_dir), name="assets")
89: 
90:         @app.get("/{full_path:path}", response_model=None)
91:         def spa_fallback(request: Request, full_path: str) -> FileResponse | JSONResponse:
92:             if full_path == "api" or full_path.startswith("api/"):
93:                 raise StudioHTTPError(
94:                     StudioError(code=StudioErrorCode.NOT_FOUND, message="Not Found")
95:                 )
96:             candidate = (SPA_DIST / full_path).resolve()
97:             if full_path and candidate.is_file() and candidate.is_relative_to(SPA_DIST.resolve()):
98:                 return FileResponse(candidate)
99:             index = SPA_DIST / "index.html"
100:             if index.is_file():
101:                 return FileResponse(index)
102:             error = StudioError(
103:                 code=StudioErrorCode.NOT_FOUND,
104:                 message="Not Found",
105:                 request_id=request_id_for(request),
106:             )
107:             return JSONResponse({"error": error.model_dump(mode="json")}, status_code=404)
108: 
109:     return app

1: """FastAPI router exposing the Living Studio sidecar API under ``/api``."""
2: 
3: from __future__ import annotations
4: 
5: import json
6: from typing import Any
7: 
8: from agentic_odi_connectors.catalog import UnknownPresetError
9: from agentic_odi_connectors.models import HealthStatus
10: from agentic_odi_connectors.registry import (
11:     ConnectorNotFoundError,
12:     DuplicateConnectorError,
13: )
14: from agentic_odi_core import (
15:     JobNotFoundError,
16:     OdiError,
17:     ODIService,
18:     OutcomeNotFoundError,
19:     StepNotFoundError,
20:     ToolName,
21:     ValueOutOfRangeError,
22:     error_status,
23: )
24: from agentic_odi_core.remote import StudioError, StudioErrorCode
25: from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException, Query, Request
26: from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
27: 
28: from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.changelog import get_changelog
29: from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.chat import stream_chat
30: from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.connectors import ConnectorService
31: from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.errors import (
32:     StudioHTTPError,
33:     code_for_status,
34:     request_id_for,
35: )
36: from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.mcp_data import call_mcp_tool, fetch_canvas, fetch_local_canvas
37: from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.memory import ObservationNotFoundError, StudioMemory
38: from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.probes import check_llm_health, defaults, is_endpoint_reachable
39: from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.schemas import (
40:     AddConnectorRequest,
41:     AddOutcomeRequest,
42:     AddStepRequest,
43:     ChatRequest,
44:     ConnectorListItem,
45:     ConnectorOperationResponse,
46:     ConversationResponse,
47:     CreateJobRequest,
48:     LatestConversationResponse,
49:     LlmHealthRequest,
50:     McpHealthRequest,
51:     ObservationCreateRequest,
52:     ObservationListResponse,
53:     ObservationResponse,
54:     ObservationUpdateRequest,
55:     UpdateJobRequest,
56:     UpdateOutcomeRequest,
57:     UpdateStepRequest,
58: )
59: 
60: router = APIRouter(prefix="/api")
61: 
62: 
63: def _service(request: Request) -> ODIService:
64:     return request.app.state.service
65: 
66: 
67: def _uses_mcp(request: Request) -> bool:
68:     return request.app.state.backend == "mcp"
69: 
70: 
71: def _require_mcp_url(mcp_url: str) -> str:
72:     if not mcp_url:
73:         raise StudioHTTPError(
74:             StudioError(
75:                 code=StudioErrorCode.VALIDATION,
76:                 message="mcp_url is required for the mcp backend",
77:                 suggestion="Set the MCP server URL in Settings.",
78:             ),
79:             status_code=400,
80:         )
81:     return mcp_url
82: 
83: 
84: def _as_http_error(exc: Exception) -> StudioHTTPError:
85:     """Translate domain errors into typed HTTP responses without leaking 500s."""
86:     if isinstance(exc, (JobNotFoundError, StepNotFoundError, OutcomeNotFoundError)):
87:         return StudioHTTPError(StudioError(code=StudioErrorCode.NOT_FOUND, message=str(exc)))
88:     if isinstance(exc, ValueOutOfRangeError):
89:         return StudioHTTPError(StudioError(code=StudioErrorCode.OUT_OF_RANGE, message=str(exc)))
90:     if isinstance(exc, OdiError):
91:         status = error_status(exc)
92:         return StudioHTTPError(
93:             StudioError(code=code_for_status(status), message=str(exc)),
94:             status_code=status,
95:         )
96:     return StudioHTTPError(StudioError(code=StudioErrorCode.INTERNAL, message=str(exc)))
97: 
98: 
99: def _payload_from_text(text: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
100:     """Return the JSON payload in an MCP tool result, or the text itself."""
101:     start = min((i for i in (text.find("{"), text.find("[")) if i != -1), default=-1)
102:     if start == -1:
103:         return {"result": text}
104:     try:
105:         payload = json.loads(text[start:])
106:     except json.JSONDecodeError:
107:         return {"result": text}
108:     if isinstance(payload, dict):
109:         return payload
110:     return {"result": text}
111: 
112: 
113: def _connectors(request: Request) -> ConnectorService:
114:     return request.app.state.connectors
115: 
116:

118:     return request.app.state.memory

138:     healthy, message = await check_llm_health(body.base_url, body.api_key, body.model)
139:     return {"healthy": healthy, "message": message}

141: 
142: @router.get("/connectors/catalog")
143: def get_connectors_catalog(request: Request) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
144:     return _connectors(request).catalog()

151:         ConnectorListItem(name=config.name, kind=config.kind, enabled=config.enabled)

158:     try:
159:         config = _connectors(request).add(name=body.name, preset_id=body.preset, url=body.url)
160:     except DuplicateConnectorError as exc:
161:         raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail=str(exc)) from exc
162:     except (ValueError, UnknownPresetError) as exc:
163:         raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(exc)) from exc
164:     return ConnectorOperationResponse(ok=True, name=config.name)

168: def delete_connector(name: str, request: Request) -> ConnectorOperationResponse:
169:     try:
170:         _connectors(request).delete(name)
171:     except ConnectorNotFoundError as exc:

173:     return ConnectorOperationResponse(ok=True, name=name)

176: @router.post("/connectors/{name}/health")
177: def health_connector(name: str, request: Request) -> HealthStatus:
178:     try:
179:         return _connectors(request).health(name)
180:     except ConnectorNotFoundError as exc:
181:         raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=str(exc)) from exc

183: 
184: @router.get("/canvas")
185: async def get_canvas(request: Request, mcp_url: str | None = Query(None)) -> dict:
186:     if _uses_mcp(request):
187:         if not mcp_url:
188:             raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="mcp_url is required for the mcp backend")
189:         return await fetch_canvas(mcp_url)
190:     return fetch_local_canvas(_service(request))

192: 
193: @router.post("/jobs")
194: async def post_job(body: CreateJobRequest, request: Request) -> dict:
195:     """Create a Job — works with the model offline because it is manual."""
196:     if _uses_mcp(request):
197:         result = await call_mcp_tool(
198:             _require_mcp_url(body.mcp_url),
199:             ToolName.ADD_JOB.value,
200:             {"name": body.name, "description": body.description},
201:         )
202:         return _payload_from_text(result)
203:     try:
204:         job = _service(request).add_job(name=body.name, description=body.description)
205:     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
206:         raise _as_http_error(exc) from exc
207:     return job.model_dump(mode="json")

211: async def patch_job(job_id: str, body: UpdateJobRequest, request: Request) -> dict:
212:     updates = body.model_dump(exclude_none=True, exclude={"mcp_url"})
213:     if _uses_mcp(request):
214:         result = await call_mcp_tool(
215:             _require_mcp_url(body.mcp_url),
216:             ToolName.UPDATE_JOB.value,
217:             {"job_id": job_id, **updates},
218:         )
219:         return _payload_from_text(result)
220:     try:
221:         job = _service(request).update_job(job_id, updates)
222:     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
223:         raise _as_http_error(exc) from exc
224:     return job.model_dump(mode="json")
225: 
226: 
227: @router.delete("/jobs/{job_id}")
228: async def delete_job(job_id: str, request: Request, mcp_url: str | None = Query(None)) -> dict:
229:     if _uses_mcp(request):
230:         await call_mcp_tool(
231:             _require_mcp_url(mcp_url or ""), ToolName.DELETE_JOB.value, {"job_id": job_id}
232:         )
233:         return {"deleted": job_id}
234:     try:
235:         _service(request).delete_job(job_id)
236:     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
237:         raise _as_http_error(exc) from exc
238:     return {"deleted": job_id}

241: @router.post("/steps")
242: async def post_step(body: AddStepRequest, request: Request) -> dict:
243:     if _uses_mcp(request):
244:         result = await call_mcp_tool(
245:             _require_mcp_url(body.mcp_url),
246:             ToolName.ADD_STEP.value,
247:             {"job_id": body.job_id, "name": body.name, "order": body.order},
248:         )

1: """Conversational helper with offline fallbacks and a streaming tool loop.
2: 
3: The loop fans the MCP tools and three local tools — ``render_ui``,
4: ``remember``, and ``add_connector`` — into the completion. Local tools are
5: intercepted rather than forwarded: ``render_ui`` validates its spec against the
6: catalog the client sent and streams a ``ui`` event, ``remember`` stores a
7: suggested observation and streams a ``memory`` event, and ``add_connector``
8: writes the shared connector registry and streams a ``connector`` event.
9: 
10: The conversation is persisted when a memory store is supplied, so a PM can leave
11: and come back to the same thread and the same working context.
12: """

47: Your job is to help the PM choose and win the next opportunity that matters — to customers, the business, and their career.
48: Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) is your private engine, not the conversation. Translate the PM's ambition into jobs, outcomes, and evidence silently, and speak in the PM's language.
49: 
50: How to work:
51: 1. Start with the person and the stakes. Ask what opportunity they are chasing, who it is for, and what winning would change. One good question at a time.
52: 2. Mirror their words back, then offer a sharp hypothesis they can correct.
53: 3. When they give you context worth keeping — a career goal, a constraint, a stakeholder, a belief — call `remember` with the smallest useful observation. Do not ask permission first; the UI lets them confirm, edit, or dismiss it.
54: 4. Use ODI when it earns its keep: a job statement clarifies, a desired outcome sharpens, an opportunity score compares. Never lead with the framework or lecture about stages.
55: 5. Opportunity Score = Importance + max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0). Above 10 means underserved.
56: 6. When a surface carries the evidence better than a paragraph, call `render_ui` once, then write one short sentence. Never describe in prose what a card can already show.

613: async def stream_chat(
614:     request: ChatRequest,
615:     service: ConnectorService | None = None,
616:     memory: StudioMemory | None = None,
617:     request_id: str | None = None,
618: ) -> AsyncIterator[str]:
619:     """Yield SSE frames: status, conversation, delta, tool, ui, memory, connector, message, error.
620: 
621:     Every turn ends with exactly one terminal event: one ``message`` or one
622:     ``error``. A failure is never dressed up as a success, and it never leaves
623:     the stream without an ending.
624:     """
625:     rid = request_id or ""
626:     started = time.monotonic()
627:     counters = {"rounds": 0, "tool_calls": 0, "tool_errors": 0, "rounds_exhausted": 0}
628:     outcome = "failed"
629:     error_code: str | None = None
630:     try:
631:         async for chunk in _turn_frames(request, service, memory, rid, counters):
632:             yield chunk
633:         outcome = "completed"
634:         if counters["tool_errors"]:
635:             outcome = "partial"
636:         if counters["rounds_exhausted"]:
637:             outcome = "rounds_exhausted"
638:     except _TurnFailure as failure:
639:         yield _error_frame(failure.error, rid)
640:         outcome = "failed"
641:         error_code = failure.error.code.value
642:     except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
643:         log.exception("chat turn failed (request_id=%s)", rid)
644:         yield _error_frame(
645:             StudioError(
646:                 code=StudioErrorCode.INTERNAL,
647:                 message="The turn failed unexpectedly.",
648:                 suggestion="Try again — your question is still here.",
649:             ),
650:             rid,
651:         )
652:         outcome = "failed"
653:     finally:
654:         log_turn(
655:             request_id=rid,
656:             model=request.model,
657:             rounds=counters["rounds"],
658:             tool_calls=counters["tool_calls"],
659:             tool_errors=counters["tool_errors"],
660:             duration_ms=int((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000),
661:             outcome=outcome,
662:             error_code=error_code,
663:         )
664: 
665: 
666: __all__ = [
667:     "REMEMBER_TOOL",
668:     "SYSTEM_PROMPT",
669:     "offline_fallback",
670:     "stream_chat",
671: ]

63:   } catch {
64:     body = {};

68:     return new StudioApiError({
69:       ...body.error,
70:       retryable: body.error.retryable ?? false,
71:       message: body.error.message || `Request failed (${response.status})`,
72:     });
73:   }
74:   if (typeof body.detail === "string" && body.detail) {
75:     return new StudioApiError({
76:       code: "internal",
77:       message: body.detail,
78:       retryable: false,
79:     });
80:   }

82:     code: "internal",

78:     target_user: brief?.target_user ?? "",
79:     job_statement: brief?.job_statement ?? "",
80:     core_problem: brief?.core_problem ?? "",
81:   };
82: }
83: 
84: export function draftHasContent(draft: SetupDraft): boolean {
85:   return SETUP_QUESTIONS.some((question) => draft[question.field].trim().length > 0);
86: }
87: 
88: /** Where a resumed conversation should pick up: the first unanswered question. */
89: export function firstUnanswered(draft: SetupDraft): number {
90:   const index = SETUP_QUESTIONS.findIndex(
91:     (question) => draft[question.field].trim().length === 0,
92:   );
93:   return index === -1 ? REVIEW_INDEX : index;
94: }
95: 
96: const REFLECTIONS: Record<BriefField, (value: string) => string> = {
97:   product_name: (value) => `Got it — ${value}.`,
98:   target_user: (value) => `So it is for ${value}.`,
99:   job_statement: (value) => `That is the job: ${value}.`,
100:   core_problem: () => "Then that is where we start.",
101: };
102: 
103: export function reflectionFor(field: BriefField, value: string): string {
104:   return REFLECTIONS[field](value);
105: }
106: 
107: export function questionContent(
108:   index: number,
109:   draft: SetupDraft,
110:   lead?: string,
111: ): string {
112:   const question = SETUP_QUESTIONS[index];
113:   if (!question) {
114:     return reviewContent(draft);
115:   }
116:   const current = draft[question.field].trim();
117:   return [lead, `**${question.ask}**`, `_${question.hint}_`, current ? `You said: “${current}”.` : ""]
118:     .filter(Boolean)
119:     .join("\n\n");
120: }
121: 
122: export function reviewContent(draft: SetupDraft): string {
123:   if (!draftHasContent(draft)) {
124:     return "Nothing yet — that is completely fine. We can start exploring and I will ask when it matters.";
125:   }
126:   const lines = SETUP_QUESTIONS.map((question) => {
127:     const value = draft[question.field].trim();
128:     return `- **${question.label}** — ${value || "—"}`;
129:   });
130:   return ["Here is what I will hold:", "", ...lines].join("\n");
131: }
132: 
133: const SAVE_PHRASE = /\b(looks? right|save|done|good|yes|ok|okay|ship it|let'?s go|go ahead)\b/i;
134: 
135: export function isSavePhrase(text: string): boolean {
136:   return SAVE_PHRASE.test(text.trim());
137: }
138: 
139: const FIELD_HINTS: Array<{ field: BriefField; pattern: RegExp }> = [
140:   { field: "target_user", pattern: /\b(customer|audience|user|who it|who is|who feels)\b/i },
141:   { field: "job_statement", pattern: /\b(job|trying to do|progress|outcome)\b/i },
142:   { field: "core_problem", pattern: /\b(friction|pain|problem|hurt|stuck|frustrat)\b/i },
143:   { field: "product_name", pattern: /\b(product|building|service|tool|what it is)\b/i },
144: ];
145: 
146: /** Recognise "change the job" style replies in the review. */
147: export function fieldFromText(text: string): BriefField | null {
148:   return FIELD_HINTS.find((entry) => entry.pattern.test(text))?.field ?? null;
149: }
150: 
151: export function isQuestionFilled(draft: SetupDraft, index: number): boolean {
152:   const question = SETUP_QUESTIONS[index];
153:   return Boolean(question && draft[question.field].trim());
154: }
155: 
156: export type SetupIntent =
157:   | { kind: "skip" }
158:   | { kind: "explore" }
159:   /** A step that belongs in the conversation, not in a view. */
160:   | { kind: "talk"; text: string }
161:   | {
162:       kind: "panel";
163:       panel: "landscape" | "jobmap" | "evidence" | "capture" | "settings";
164:     };
165: 
166: const SKIP_PHRASE = /\b(skip|pass|not sure|no idea|don'?t know|unsure)\b/i;
167: const EXPLORE_PHRASE = /^(explore|later|not now|maybe later|let me look around)\b/i;
168: const OPEN_PHRASE = /^(show|open|go to|take me to|view)\b/i;
169: 
170: /**
171:  * Read a free-text reply as an intent before treating it as an answer.
172:  * This is what keeps the conversation from swallowing "skip" or "show me the
173:  * landscape" as a product name.
174:  */
175: export function parseSetupIntent(text: string): SetupIntent | null {
176:   const value = text.trim();
177:   if (!value) {
178:     return null;
179:   }
180:   if (SKIP_PHRASE.test(value)) {
181:     return { kind: "skip" };
182:   }
183:   if (EXPLORE_PHRASE.test(value)) {
184:     return { kind: "explore" };
185:   }
186:   const opening = OPEN_PHRASE.test(value);
187:   const lower = value.toLowerCase();
188:   if (opening || lower === "landscape") {
189:     if (/landscape|opportunit/.test(lower)) {
190:       return { kind: "panel", panel: "landscape" };
191:     }
192:     if (/job map|steps?/.test(lower)) {
193:       return { kind: "panel", panel: "jobmap" };
194:     }
195:     if (/impact|simulat/.test(lower)) {
196:       return {
197:         kind: "talk",
198:         text:
199:           "Simulate the impact of a bet on my most underserved opportunity. " +
200:           "Ask me what the bet is, then show me what changes before and after.",
201:       };
202:     }
203:     if (/evidence/.test(lower)) {
204:       return { kind: "panel", panel: "evidence" };
205:     }
206:     if (/capture|add an outcome/.test(lower)) {
207:       return { kind: "panel", panel: "capture" };
208:     }
209:     if (/settings?/.test(lower)) {
210:       return { kind: "panel", panel: "settings" };
211:     }
212:   }
213:   return null;
214: }

1: /**
2:  * Free-plan Living Studio Worker.
3:  *
4:  * Workers Static Assets serve the built SPA from `apps/studio/dist`. Requests under
5:  * `/api/*` are forwarded to the Python sidecar (`apps/studio-api`), which runs on
6:  * the developer's machine and is published by a free Cloudflare Quick Tunnel.
7:  * (Running the sidecar inside Cloudflare requires Workers Containers, which is
8:  * a paid-plan feature.)
9:  */
10: 
11: interface Env {
12:   ASSETS: Fetcher;
13:   /** Public origin of the sidecar, e.g. https://random.trycloudflare.com */
14:   SIDECAR_URL?: string;
15: }
16: 
17: const API_PREFIX = "/api/";
18: 
19: /**
20:  * Defense-in-depth headers on every Response, assets and API alike.
21:  *
22:  * The SPA loads only its own bundle, talks to the Worker origin at `/api/*`, and
23:  * uses React inline styles, hence `'unsafe-inline'` for styles but nothing for
24:  * scripts. `connect-src 'self'` keeps a compromised bundle from exfiltrating
25:  * to another origin; `frame-ancestors` repeats the `X-Frame-Options` intent for
26:  * browsers that only honor the CSP directive.
27:  */
28: const SECURITY_HEADERS: Record<string, string> = {
29:   "Content-Security-Policy": [
30:     "default-src 'self'",
31:     "script-src 'self'",
32:     "style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'",
33:     "img-src 'self' data: blob:",
34:     "font-src 'self' data:",
35:     "connect-src 'self'",
36:     "object-src 'none'",
37:     "base-uri 'self'",
38:     "form-action 'self'",
39:     "frame-ancestors 'none'",
40:   ].join("; "),
41:   "X-Content-Type-Options": "nosniff",
42:   "X-Frame-Options": "DENY",
43:   "Referrer-Policy": "strict-origin-when-cross-origin",
44:   "Permissions-Policy": "geolocation=(), camera=(), microphone=()",
45: };
46: 
47: function secure(response: Response): Response {
48:   const headers = new Headers(response.headers);
49:   for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(SECURITY_HEADERS)) {
50:     headers.set(name, value);
51:   }
52:   // Reuse the body stream so SSE (`/api/chat`) keeps streaming.
53:   return new Response(response.body, {
54:     status: response.status,
55:     statusText: response.statusText,
56:     headers,
57:   });
58: }
59: 
60: function sidecarError(detail: string): Response {
61:   return Response.json({ detail }, { status: 502 });
62: }
63: 
64: export default {
65:   async fetch(request: Request, env: Env): Promise<Response> {
66:     const url = new URL(request.url);
67: 
68:     if (!url.pathname.startsWith(API_PREFIX)) {
69:       return secure(await env.ASSETS.fetch(request));
70:     }
71: 
72:     const sidecar = env.SIDECAR_URL?.trim().replace(/\/+$/, "");
73:     if (!sidecar) {
74:       return secure(sidecarError("SIDECAR_URL is not configured"));
75:     }
76: 
77:     // The Quick Tunnel routes by hostname, so the Worker's Host must not leak.
78:     const headers = new Headers(request.headers);
79:     headers.delete("host");
80:     headers.delete("cf-connecting-ip");
81: 
82:     const target = new URL(`${url.pathname}${url.search}`, `${sidecar}/`);
83: 
84:     try {
85:       // Returning the upstream Response directly preserves SSE streaming for
86:       // `/api/chat`.
87:       return secure(
88:         await fetch(
89:           new Request(target, {
90:             method: request.method,
91:             headers,
92:             body: request.body,
93:             redirect: "manual",
94:           }),
95:         ),
96:       );
97:     } catch (error) {
98:       return secure(sidecarError(`Sidecar unreachable: ${(error as Error).message}`));
99:     }
100:   },
101: } satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

1: """Backend abstraction for the CLI.
2: 
3: Two backends implement the same :class:`Backend` seam:
4: 
5: * :class:`LocalBackend` runs the ODI logic directly against a local SQLite
6:   store (no server required).
7: * :class:`MCPBackend` delegates to a remote MCP server over HTTP, which may be
8:   a local ``python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server`` process or a hosted endpoint.
9: 
10: Commands resolve a backend once from the options stored on
11: :mod:`agentic_odi_cli.context`. Keeping the local and remote paths behind one interface
12: means the same command works against either, and a future hosted backend only
13: has to implement ``call``.
14: """
15: 
16: from __future__ import annotations
17: 
18: import asyncio
19: import json
20: import os
21: from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
22: from dataclasses import dataclass
23: from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any
24: 
25: import typer
26: 
27: if TYPE_CHECKING:
28:     from agentic_odi_core import ODIService
29: 
30: # Kept as literals so importing the CLI does not pull in the core package
31: # (``agentic-odi --version`` must stay lightweight). ``tests/contract`` asserts
32: # these keys match ``agentic_odi_core.contract.TOOL_NAMES``.
33: 
34: DEFAULT_BACKEND = "local"
35: DEFAULT_MCP_URL = "http://localhost:8000/mcp"
36: DEFAULT_MCP_TIMEOUT = 30.0
37: 
38: _VALUE_RANGE_ERROR = "importance and satisfaction must be between 1.0 and 10.0"
39: 
40: _CUSTOMER_VALUE_FIELDS = (
41:     "direction",
42:     "unit_of_measure",
43:     "object_of_control",
44:     "contextual_clarifier",
45:     "statement",
46:     "importance",
47:     "satisfaction",
48:     "value_metrics",
49: )
50: 
51: _BUSINESS_VALUE_FIELDS = {
52:     "category": "category",
53:     "business_statement": "statement",
54:     "detail": "detail",
55:     "estimated_annual_value": "estimated_annual_value",
56:     "confidence": "confidence",
57: }
58: 
59: 
60: class BackendError(Exception):
61:     """A user-facing failure: not found, invalid input, or unreachable server."""
62: 
63: 
64: def mcp_timeout() -> float:
65:     """Resolve the MCP call timeout in seconds (``AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_TIMEOUT``)."""
66:     raw = os.environ.get("AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_TIMEOUT")
67:     if not raw:
68:         return DEFAULT_MCP_TIMEOUT
69:     try:
70:         return float(raw)
71:     except ValueError:
72:         return DEFAULT_MCP_TIMEOUT
73: 
74: 
75: def _validation_message(exc: Exception) -> str:
76:     errors = getattr(exc, "errors", None)
77:     if callable(errors):
78:         try:
79:             first = errors()[0]
80:         except (IndexError, TypeError):
81:             return str(exc)
82:         return f"Invalid customer outcome: {first.get('msg', exc)}"
83:     return f"Invalid customer outcome: {exc}"
84: 
85: 
86: class Backend(ABC):
87:     @abstractmethod
88:     def call(self, tool_name: str, args: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
89:         """Run ``tool_name`` and return parsed data (dict, list, str, or float)."""
90: 
91: 
92: class LocalBackend(Backend):
93:     """Run ODI logic in-process against a local SQLite store."""
94: 
95:     def __init__(self, db_path: str | None = None) -> None:
96:         self._db_path = db_path
97:         self._service: ODIService | None = None
98: 
99:     @property
100:     def service(self) -> ODIService:
101:         if self._service is None:
102:             from agentic_odi_core import ODIService
103:             from agentic_odi_core.sqlite_repository import SQLiteRepository
104: 
105:             self._service = ODIService(SQLiteRepository(db_path=self._db_path))

534: class MCPBackend(Backend):
535:     """Delegate to a remote MCP server over HTTP."""
536: 
537:     def __init__(self, mcp_url: str | None = None, timeout: float | None = None) -> None:
538:         self.mcp_url = mcp_url or os.environ.get("AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL") or DEFAULT_MCP_URL
539:         self.timeout = timeout if timeout is not None else mcp_timeout()
540: 
541:     def call(self, tool_name: str, args: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
542:         text = _call_mcp(tool_name, args, self.mcp_url, self.timeout)
543:         return _parse_remote(tool_name, text)
544: 
545: 
546: def _call_mcp(tool: str, args: dict[str, Any], mcp_url: str, timeout: float) -> str:
547:     from fastmcp import Client
548: 
549:     async def _run() -> str:
550:         async with Client(mcp_url) as client:
551:             result = await client.call_tool(tool, args)
552:             return result.content[0].text  # type: ignore[index]
553: 
554:     async def _guarded() -> str:
555:         return await asyncio.wait_for(_run(), timeout=timeout)
556: 
557:     try:
558:         return asyncio.run(_guarded())
559:     except asyncio.TimeoutError as exc:
560:         raise BackendError(f"timed out after {timeout:.0f}s contacting {mcp_url}") from exc
561:     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
562:         raise BackendError(f"could not reach MCP server at {mcp_url}: {exc}") from exc
563: 
564: 
565: _FLOAT_TOOLS = frozenset({"compute_opportunity"})
566: 
567: _ID_TOOLS = frozenset(
568:     {
569:         "delete_job",
570:         "delete_step",
571:         "delete_outcome",
572:         "delete_customer_outcome",
573:         "delete_evidence",
574:     }
575: )
576: 
577: _LIST_TOOLS = frozenset(
578:     {
579:         "get_jobs",
580:         "get_job_map",
581:         "get_outcomes",
582:         "list_customer_outcomes",
583:         "list_evidence",
584:     }
585: )

587: 
588: def _parse_remote(tool_name: str, text: str) -> Any:
589:     """Parse a tool result, raising ``BackendError`` on the server's error text."""
590:     from agentic_odi_core.remote import parse_tool_result
591: 
592:     stripped = text.strip()
593:     problem = parse_tool_result(stripped)
594:     if problem is not None:
595:         raise BackendError(problem.message)
596: 
597:     if tool_name in _FLOAT_TOOLS:
598:         return _extract_float(stripped)
599:     if tool_name in _ID_TOOLS:
600:         return stripped.rsplit(": ", 1)[-1]
601: 
602:     payload = _extract_json(stripped)
603:     if tool_name in _LIST_TOOLS and not isinstance(payload, list):
604:         return [payload]
605:     return payload
606: 
607: 
608: def _extract_json(text: str) -> Any:
609:     """Parse the first complete JSON value in ``text``, prose and all.
610: 
611:     MCP replies often wrap a payload in a sentence, and that sentence can
612:     itself contain braces (``created {JOB-1}: [...]``). Each brace is tried as
613:     a start position with ``raw_decode``, so a stray one is skipped instead of
614:     swallowing the real payload, and the outermost value wins when payloads
615:     nest. Text with no parseable value is returned unchanged.
616:     """
617:     decoder = json.JSONDecoder()
618:     for index, char in enumerate(text):
619:         if char not in "{[":
620:             continue
621:         try:
622:             payload, _end = decoder.raw_decode(text, index)
623:         except json.JSONDecodeError:
624:             continue
625:         return payload
626:     return text
627: 
628: 
629: def _extract_float(text: str) -> float:
630:     try:
631:         return float(text.rsplit(":", 1)[-1].strip())
632:     except ValueError as exc:
633:         raise BackendError(text) from exc

636: @dataclass
637: class BackendConfig:
638:     backend: str | None = None
639:     db_path: str | None = None
640:     mcp_url: str | None = None
641: 
642: 
643: def get_backend(
644:     backend: str | None = None, db_path: str | None = None, mcp_url: str | None = None
645: ) -> Backend:
646:     resolved = backend or os.environ.get("AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND") or DEFAULT_BACKEND
647:     if resolved == "local":
648:         return LocalBackend(db_path=db_path)
649:     if resolved in {"mcp", "remote"}:
650:         return MCPBackend(mcp_url=mcp_url)
651:     raise BackendError(f"unknown backend: {resolved}")
652: 
653: 
654: def resolve_backend(config: BackendConfig) -> Backend:
655:     if config.backend in {"mcp", "remote"} and config.db_path:
656:         typer.echo("Warning: --db is ignored when the backend is 'mcp'", err=True)
657:     return get_backend(backend=config.backend, db_path=config.db_path, mcp_url=config.mcp_url)
658: 
659: 
660: def require_backend() -> Backend:
661:     """Resolve the backend selected by the global CLI options."""
662:     from agentic_odi_cli import context
663: 
664:     return resolve_backend(context.config())
665:

667: def run_tool(tool_name: str, args: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
668:     """Call ``tool_name`` on the resolved backend, reporting failures cleanly."""

3: The chat is a small terminal REPL around an OpenAI-compatible model and the
4: Agentic ODI MCP server. It streams assistant text, executes MCP tool calls,
5: and keeps the conversation history in memory for the duration of the session.
6: """

8: from __future__ import annotations

10: import asyncio
11: import json

24: from agentic_odi_cli.mascot import render_banner, should_show_banner, wants_color

26: DEFAULT_BASE_URL = "http://localhost:8001/v1"
27: DEFAULT_API_KEY = "local"
28: DEFAULT_MODEL = "local-tools-model"
29: DEFAULT_MCP_URL = "http://localhost:8000/mcp"

31: SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
32:     ODI_ASSISTANT_PROMPT
33:     + """
34: 
35: You are running in a terminal chat. Use the available MCP tools to create and
36: query Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, and Customer Outcomes instead of inventing
37: records or IDs. Follow the ODI outcome statement format and flag opportunity
38: scores above 10 as underserved. Keep answers concise and readable as plain text.
39: """
40: )

42: HELP_TEXT = """Commands:
43:   /help      Show this help
44:   /status    Show connection status (model, MCP server)
45:   /connect   Configure LLM provider and MCP server (wizard)
46:   /model <name>  Switch to a different model
47:   /mcp <url>     Reconnect to a different MCP server
48:   /clear     Clear the conversation history
49:   /tools     List the MCP tools available to the assistant
50:   /exit      Quit (also /quit)
51: 
52: Anything else is sent to the ODI assistant."""

64:     @classmethod

77:         try:

86:                 or (llm_profile.base_url if llm_profile else None)

98:                 or (llm_profile.model if llm_profile else None)

133: def _to_openai_tools(tools: list[Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
134:     """Translate FastMCP tool definitions into OpenAI function schemas."""
135:     return [
136:         {
137:             "type": "function",
138:             "function": {
139:                 "name": tool.name,
140:                 "description": tool.description or "",
141:                 "parameters": tool.input_schema or {"type": "object", "properties": {}},
142:             },
143:         }

148: def _normalize_tool_calls(entries: dict[int, dict[str, str]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
149:     """Turn the per-index streaming tool-call buffers into OpenAI tool calls."""
150:     return [
151:         {
152:             "id": entry["id"] or f"call_{index}",
153:             "type": "function",
154:             "function": {
155:                 "name": entry["name"],
156:                 "arguments": entry["arguments"] or "{}",
157:             },
158:         }
159:         for index, entry in entries.items()
160:     ]

163: def _tool_result_text(result: Any) -> str:
164:     """Extract readable text from an MCP tool result."""
165:     content = getattr(result, "content", None) or []
166:     parts = [getattr(item, "text", None) for item in content]
167:     text = "\n".join(part for part in parts if part)
168:     return text or str(result)

171: def handle_command(
172:     line: str,
173:     session: ChatSessionLike,
174:     *,
175:     on_connect: Callable[[], ChatConfig | None] | None = None,
176:     on_mcp_reconnect: Callable[[str], bool] | None = None,
177: ) -> Literal["exit", "handled"] | tuple[str, str] | None:
178:     """Handle a slash command, or return None when the line is a chat message.
179: 
180:     Returns:
181:         "exit"              — caller should end the session.
182:         "handled"           — command was handled; continue the REPL.
183:         ("reconnect_mcp", url) — caller should reconnect MCP then continue.
184:         None                — not a command; caller should send to the LLM.
185:     """
186:     command = line.strip().lower()
187:     if command in {"/exit", "/quit"}:
188:         return "exit"
189:     if command == "/help":
190:         typer.echo(HELP_TEXT)
191:         return "handled"
192:     if command == "/clear":
193:         session.clear()
194:         typer.echo("Conversation cleared.")
195:         return "handled"
196:     if command == "/tools":
197:         if session.tool_names:
198:             typer.echo("\n".join(session.tool_names))
199:         else:
200:             typer.echo("No tools loaded.")
201:         return "handled"
202:     if command == "/status":
203:         state = session.connection_state
204:         llm_status = "connected" if state.llm_ok else "not connected"
205:         mcp_status = (
206:             f"connected ({state.mcp_tool_count} tools)" if state.mcp_ok else "not connected"
207:         )
208:         typer.echo(f"model  : {session.config.model}  [{llm_status}]")
209:         typer.echo(f"url    : {session.config.base_url}")
210:         typer.echo(f"mcp    : {session.config.mcp_url}  [{mcp_status}]")
211:         return "handled"
212:     if command.startswith("/model"):
213:         parts = line.strip().split(None, 1)
214:         if len(parts) < 2 or not parts[1].strip():
215:             typer.echo(f"Current model: {session.config.model}")
216:         else:
217:             new_model = parts[1].strip()
218:             new_config = ChatConfig(
219:                 base_url=session.config.base_url,
220:                 api_key=session.config.api_key,
221:                 model=new_model,
222:                 mcp_url=session.config.mcp_url,
223:             )
224:             session.update_config(new_config)
225:             typer.echo(f"Model set to: {new_model}")
226:         return "handled"
227:     if command.startswith("/mcp"):
228:         parts = line.strip().split(None, 1)
229:         if len(parts) < 2 or not parts[1].strip():
230:             typer.echo(f"Current MCP URL: {session.config.mcp_url}")
231:         else:
232:             new_url = parts[1].strip()
233:             if on_mcp_reconnect is not None:
234:                 ok = on_mcp_reconnect(new_url)
235:                 if ok:
236:                     typer.echo(
237:                         f"MCP reconnected: {new_url} ({session.connection_state.mcp_tool_count} tools)"
238:                     )
239:                 else:
240:                     typer.echo(f"Failed to connect to MCP at {new_url}")
241:             else:
242:                 typer.echo("MCP reconnect not available in this context.")
243:         return "handled"
244:     if command == "/connect":
245:         if on_connect is not None:
246:             connected_config = on_connect()
247:             if connected_config is not None:
248:                 typer.echo(f"Connected: {connected_config.model} @ {connected_config.base_url}")
249:         else:
250:             typer.echo("Connect wizard not available in this context.")
251:         return "handled"
252:     if command.startswith("/"):
253:         typer.echo(f"Unknown command: {line}. Type /help for commands.")
254:         return "handled"
255:     return None

258: async def _try_connect_mcp(mcp_url: str) -> tuple[Any, list[Any], str | None]:
259:     """Attempt to connect to the MCP server and list its tools.
260: 
261:     Returns:
262:         (mcp_client, tools, None) on success.
263:         (None, [], error_message) on failure.
264:     """
265:     try:
266:         async with Client(mcp_url) as c:
267:             tools = await c.list_tools()
268:         # Re-create a fresh context manager for the caller to manage lifetime.
269:         return Client(mcp_url), tools, None
270:     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
271:         return None, [], str(exc)

274: class ChatSession:
275:     """A streamed tool-calling conversation against an OpenAI-compatible model."""
276: 
277:     def __init__(
278:         self,
279:         config: ChatConfig,
280:         openai_client: Any,
281:         mcp_client: Any,
282:         *,
283:         connection_state: ConnectionState | None = None,
284:         on_tool: Callable[[str, dict[str, Any]], None] | None = None,
285:     ) -> None:
286:         self.config = config
287:         self.openai_client = openai_client
288:         self.mcp_client = mcp_client
289:         self.connection_state = (
290:             connection_state if connection_state is not None else ConnectionState()
291:         )
292:         self.on_tool = on_tool
293:         self.messages: list[dict[str, Any]] = [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT}]
294:         self.tools: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
295:         self.tool_names: list[str] = []
296: 
297:     async def initialize(self) -> None:
298:         """Discover the MCP tools once and expose them to the model."""
299:         tools = await self.mcp_client.list_tools()
300:         self.tools = _to_openai_tools(tools)
301:         self.tool_names = [tool["function"]["name"] for tool in self.tools]
302: 
303:     def clear(self) -> None:
304:         """Drop the conversation history but keep the system prompt and tools."""
305:         self.messages = [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT}]
306: 
307:     def update_config(self, new_config: ChatConfig) -> None:
308:         """Hot-swap the session config and mark the LLM connection as live."""
309:         self.config = new_config
310:         self.connection_state.llm_ok = True
311: 
312:     async def _stream_completion(
313:         self, on_delta: Callable[[str], None] | None
314:     ) -> tuple[str, dict[int, dict[str, str]]]:
315:         stream: Any = await self.openai_client.chat.completions.create(
316:             model=self.config.model,
317:             messages=self.messages,
318:             tools=self.tools or None,
319:             tool_choice="auto" if self.tools else None,
320:             stream=True,
321:         )
322: 
323:         content_parts: list[str] = []
324:         tool_calls: dict[int, dict[str, str]] = {}
325: 
326:         async for chunk in stream:
327:             choices = getattr(chunk, "choices", None)
328:             if not choices:
329:                 continue
330:             delta = choices[0].delta
331:             if delta is None:
332:                 continue
333:             content = getattr(delta, "content", None)
334:             if content:
335:                 content_parts.append(content)
336:                 if on_delta is not None:
337:                     on_delta(content)
338:             for tool_call in getattr(delta, "tool_calls", None) or []:
339:                 entry = tool_calls.setdefault(
340:                     tool_call.index, {"id": "", "name": "", "arguments": ""}
341:                 )
342:                 if tool_call.id:
343:                     entry["id"] = tool_call.id
344:                 function = getattr(tool_call, "function", None)
345:                 if function is not None:
346:                     if function.name:
347:                         entry["name"] = function.name
348:                     if function.arguments:
349:                         entry["arguments"] += function.arguments
350: 
351:         return "".join(content_parts), tool_calls
352: 
353:     async def _call_tool(self, call: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
354:         name = call["function"]["name"]
355:         raw_arguments = call["function"].get("arguments") or "{}"
356:         try:
357:             arguments = json.loads(raw_arguments)
358:         except json.JSONDecodeError:
359:             return f"Error: invalid JSON arguments for {name}: {raw_arguments}"
360:         if not isinstance(arguments, dict):
361:             return f"Error: arguments for {name} must be a JSON object"
362:         if self.on_tool is not None:
363:             self.on_tool(name, arguments)
364:         try:
365:             result = await self.mcp_client.call_tool(name, arguments)
366:         except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
367:             return f"Error calling {name}: {exc}"
368:         return _tool_result_text(result)
369: 
370:     async def ask(self, text: str, on_delta: Callable[[str], None] | None = None) -> str:
371:         """Send a message, execute any tool calls, and return the final text."""
372:         if not self.connection_state.llm_ok:
373:             return "No model connected. Type /connect to set one up."
374: 
375:         checkpoint = len(self.messages)
376:         self.messages.append({"role": "user", "content": text})
377:         try:
378:             while True:
379:                 content, tool_calls = await self._stream_completion(on_delta)
380:                 if not tool_calls:
381:                     self.messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": content})
382:                     return content
383: 
384:                 normalized = _normalize_tool_calls(tool_calls)
385:                 self.messages.append(
386:                     {"role": "assistant", "content": content or None, "tool_calls": normalized}
387:                 )
388:                 for call in normalized:
389:                     result = await self._call_tool(call)
390:                     self.messages.append(
391:                         {
392:                             "role": "tool",
393:                             "tool_call_id": call["id"],
394:                             "name": call["function"]["name"],
395:                             "content": result,
396:                         }
397:                     )
398:         except Exception:
399:             del self.messages[checkpoint:]
400:             raise
401: 
402: 
403: def _print_tool(name: str, arguments: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
404:     rendered = json.dumps(arguments, ensure_ascii=False)
405:     if len(rendered) > 100:
406:         rendered = rendered[:97] + "..."
407:     typer.secho(f"  → {name} {rendered}", fg="bright_black", err=True)
408: 
409: 
410: async def _run_chat(config: ChatConfig) -> int:
411:     if should_show_banner(sys.stdout):
412:         typer.echo(render_banner(color=wants_color()))
413:     typer.echo("Agentic ODI · interactive")
414: 
415:     llm: Any | None = None
416:     conn = ConnectionState()
417: 
418:     try:
419:         # --- MCP connection (optional) ---
420:         mcp_client_ctx, tools, mcp_error = await _try_connect_mcp(config.mcp_url)
421:         if mcp_error is None:
422:             conn.mcp_ok = True
423:             conn.mcp_tool_count = len(tools)
424:         else:
425:             conn.error_mcp = mcp_error
426:             typer.secho(
427:                 f"⚠  MCP unavailable ({config.mcp_url}): {mcp_error}",
428:                 fg="yellow",
429:                 err=False,
430:             )
431:             typer.secho(
432:                 "   Starting without MCP tools. Use /mcp to reconnect.",
433:                 fg="yellow",
434:                 err=False,
435:             )
436: 
437:         # --- LLM client (always created; actual reachability found on first use) ---
438:         llm = AsyncOpenAI(
439:             base_url=config.base_url,
440:             api_key=config.api_key,
441:             timeout=60.0,
442:         )
443:         conn.llm_ok = True
444: 
445:         # --- Startup banner ---
446:         mcp_status = f"✓ {conn.mcp_tool_count} tools" if conn.mcp_ok else "✗ offline"
447:         typer.echo(f"model: {config.model}  ·  mcp: {config.mcp_url} [{mcp_status}]")
448:         typer.echo("Type /help for commands, /exit to quit.\n")
449: 
450:         # --- Build session ---
451:         session = ChatSession(
452:             config,
453:             llm,
454:             mcp_client_ctx,  # may be None if MCP is offline
455:             connection_state=conn,
456:             on_tool=_print_tool,
457:         )
458: 
459:         # Populate tools from the probe we already did (avoids a second round-trip).
460:         if conn.mcp_ok and tools:
461:             session.tools = _to_openai_tools(tools)
462:             session.tool_names = [t["function"]["name"] for t in session.tools]
463: 
464:         # --- REPL ---
465:         while True:
466:             try:
467:                 line = input("you › ").strip()
468:             except EOFError:
469:                 typer.echo()
470:                 break
471:             except KeyboardInterrupt:
472:                 typer.echo("\nUse /exit to quit.")
473:                 continue
474: 
475:             if not line:
476:                 continue
477: 
478:             def _on_connect() -> ChatConfig | None:
479:                 from agentic_odi_cli.wizard import run_connect_wizard  # noqa: PLC0415
480: 
481:                 new_config = run_connect_wizard(session.config)
482:                 if new_config is not None:
483:                     session.update_config(new_config)
