486:             def _on_mcp_reconnect(new_url: str) -> bool:
487:                 """Run MCP reconnect in a separate thread (avoids nested event loops)."""
488:                 import concurrent.futures  # noqa: PLC0415
489: 
490:                 async def _reconnect() -> bool:
491:                     _, new_tools, err = await _try_connect_mcp(new_url)
492:                     if err is not None:
493:                         return False
494:                     new_config = ChatConfig(
495:                         base_url=session.config.base_url,
496:                         api_key=session.config.api_key,
497:                         model=session.config.model,
498:                         mcp_url=new_url,
499:                     )
500:                     session.update_config(new_config)
501:                     session.mcp_client = Client(new_url)
502:                     session.tools = _to_openai_tools(new_tools)
503:                     session.tool_names = [t["function"]["name"] for t in session.tools]
504:                     session.connection_state.mcp_ok = True
505:                     session.connection_state.mcp_tool_count = len(new_tools)

508:                 with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) as executor:
509:                     future = executor.submit(asyncio.run, _reconnect())
510:                     return future.result()

512:             action = handle_command(
513:                 line, session, on_connect=_on_connect, on_mcp_reconnect=_on_mcp_reconnect
514:             )

517:             if action == "handled":

520:             typer.secho("odi › ", fg="green", bold=True, nl=False)

541:         if llm is not None:

53: def is_endpoint_reachable(url: str, timeout: float = 0.3) -> bool:
54:     """Quick socket check to verify a port is open without hanging on HTTP reads."""
55:     try:
56:         parsed = urlparse(url)
57:         host = parsed.hostname or "localhost"
58:         port = parsed.port or (443 if parsed.scheme == "https" else 80)
59:         with socket.create_connection((host, port), timeout=timeout):
60:             return True

66:     message = str(exc)
67:     lower = message.lower()
68:     connection_indicators = [
69:         "connection error",
70:         "connection aborted",
71:         "failed to establish a new connection",
72:         "timed out",
73:         "timeout",
74:         "connection refused",
75:     ]
76:     if any(indicator in lower for indicator in connection_indicators):

742:       const history: ChatMessage[] = [...messages, { role: "user", content: trimmed }];
743:       const assistantIndex = history.length;
744:       setMessages([...history, { role: "assistant", content: "", parts: [] }]);
745:       setStreaming(true);
746:       setThinkingPhase("health_check");
747:       setOfflineReply(false);
748:       setToolActivity([]);
749: 
750:       const controller = new AbortController();
751:       abortRef.current = controller;
752: 
753:       let content = "";
754:       let parts: ChatPart[] = [];
755:       let failure: StudioError | null = null;
756:       let terminal = false;
757:       let stopped = false;
758: 
759:       // Prose is appended to the open text part; a surface opens a new one, so
760:       // the transcript keeps the agent's order instead of gathering all prose
761:       // above all cards.
762:       const appendText = (text: string) => {
763:         if (!text) {
764:           return;
765:         }
766:         content += text;
767:         const last = parts[parts.length - 1];
768:         parts =
769:           last?.kind === "text"
770:             ? [...parts.slice(0, -1), { kind: "text", text: last.text + text }]
771:             : [...parts, { kind: "text", text }];
772:       };
773: 
774:       const publish = () => {
775:         setMessages((prev) => {
776:           const next = [...prev];
777:           next[assistantIndex] = {
778:             role: "assistant",
779:             content,
780:             parts: [...parts],
781:             ...(failure ? { error: failure, retryText: trimmed } : {}),
782:           };
783:           return next;
784:         });
785:       };
786: 
787:       const handleEvent = (event: RawSseEvent) => {
788:         switch (event.event) {
789:           case "status": {
790:             const phase = String(event.data.phase ?? "");
791:             setThinkingPhase(phase);
792:             if (phase === "offline") {
793:               setOfflineReply(true);
794:             }
795:             break;
796:           }
797:           case "delta": {
798:             appendText(String(event.data.text ?? ""));
799:             publish();
800:             break;
801:           }
802:           case "ui": {
803:             // Validate again on arrival: the connection is local but the
804:             // renderer must never trust a shape it has not checked.
805:             const parsed = parseUiSpec(event.data.spec, catalogManifest());
806:             if (parsed.ok) {
807:               parts = [
808:                 ...parts,
809:                 { kind: "ui", id: String(event.data.id ?? `ui-${parts.length}`), node: parsed.node },
810:               ];
811:               publish();
812:             }
813:             break;
814:           }
815:           case "tool":
816:             setToolActivity((prev) => [
817:               ...prev,
818:               {
819:                 name: String(event.data.name ?? ""),
820:                 status: String(event.data.status ?? ""),
821:                 preview: event.data.preview ? String(event.data.preview) : undefined,
822:               },
823:             ]);
824:             break;
825:           case "message": {
826:             terminal = true;
827:             content = String(event.data.content ?? content);
828:             const hasSurfaces = parts.some((part) => part.kind === "ui");
829:             if (!hasSurfaces) {
830:               parts = content ? [{ kind: "text", text: content }] : [];
831:             }
832:             publish();
833:             break;
834:           }
835:           case "conversation": {
836:             const id = String(event.data.id ?? "");
837:             if (id) {
838:               setConversationId(id);
839:             }
840:             break;
841:           }
842:           case "memory": {
843:             const observation = event.data.observation as Observation | undefined;
844:             if (observation?.id) {
845:               setMemory((prev) =>
846:                 prev.some((item) => item.id === observation.id)
847:                   ? prev.map((item) => (item.id === observation.id ? observation : item))
848:                   : [...prev, observation],
849:               );
850:             }
851:             break;
852:           }
853:           case "canvas_dirty":
854:             void refreshCanvas();
855:             break;
856:           case "connector": {
857:             if (String(event.data.status ?? "") === "error") {
858:               const reason = String(event.data.error ?? "The connector could not be added.");
859:               setMessages((prev) => [
860:                 ...prev,
861:                 { role: "notice", content: `Connector failed: ${reason}` },
862:               ]);
863:             } else {
864:               setConnectorSuggestions((prev) => {
865:                 const id = String(event.data?.preset ?? event.data?.name ?? "");
866:                 if (!id || prev.includes(id)) {
867:                   return prev;
868:                 }
869:                 return [...prev, id];
870:               });
871:             }
872:             void refreshConnectors();
873:             break;
874:           }
875:           case "error": {
876:             terminal = true;
877:             failure = readStudioError(event.data.error);
878:             publish();
879:             break;
880:           }
881:           default:
882:             break;
883:         }
884:       };

886:       try {
887:         await streamChat(
888:           {
889:             base_url: settings.base_url,
890:             api_key: settings.api_key,
891:             model: settings.model_name,
892:             mcp_url: settings.mcp_url,

929:           publish();
930:         }
931:         setStreaming(false);
932:         setThinkingPhase(null);
933:         abortRef.current = null;
934:       }

I've mapped the error handling across the full stack. Here's my research and proposed plan. I'm in read-only plan mode, so nothing is changed yet — implementation waits on your approval (per the superpowers hard gate: no build until the design is signed off).

## Current state (what's already good)

- `packages/core/.../errors.py` — clean `OdiError` hierarchy with `error_status()` mapping. ✅
- `packages/core/.../remote.py` — `StudioError` model + `parse_tool_result()` classifies MCP text errors with code/suggestion/retryable. ✅
- `apps/studio-api/.../studio/errors.py` — one-error-body (`{"error": StudioError}`), request-id middleware, unhandled handler that logs without leaking internals. ✅
- `apps/studio-api/.../studio/chat.py` — graceful offline fallback when the LLM is unreachable; `_TurnFailure` ends streams with one `error` event; silent-stream-end is caught. ✅
- SPA: `FailurePanel` (message/detail/suggestion/retry), `OfflineNotice` for model-offline ("Working by hand…"), `CanvasState` union (`loading|ready|empty|error`), connector `presetError`/`connectorsError`. ✅
- CLI `backend.py` — `BackendError` + red "Error:" reporting; MCP connection failures name the URL. ✅

## The confirmed gap: no good "sidecar is not running" statement

This is what you flagged, and it's real:

- When the sidecar is down, `StudioContext.boot()` sets `sidecarReachable = false`, but **nothing renders a persistent, human-friendly statement about it**. The canvas fetch then fails and surfaces a generic `asStudioError` → `"Something went wrong."` / `code: "internal"`, with no suggestion and no hint how to start the sidecar (`python scripts/dev.py` / `npm --prefix apps/studio run dev:full`).
- The Cloudflare worker returns legacy `{"detail": …}` (not the `{"error": StudioError}` shape) on `SIDECAR_URL` unset / unreachable, so the SPA can't render a structured FailurePanel with retry.
- There's no `OfflineNotice`-equivalent for the sidecar itself (only for the model).

## Other weaknesses worth fixing in the same pass

| Area | Problem |
|------|---------|
| Human-friendly messages | `asStudioError` fetch-failure fallback is always `"Something went wrong."` — no classification by status (network vs 404 vs 429 vs 502). `unhandled_error_handler` tells the user "the team has been notified" but doesn't surface the request id they could reference. |
| Graceful degradation | Canvas hard-errors to `kind: "error"` when the sidecar is down instead of showing stale cache with a "stale data" banner. |
| Consistency | `router.py` mixes `StudioHTTPError` (`{"error":…}`) with raw `HTTPException` (legacy `{"detail":…}`) in connectors/memory routes. MCP server returns unstructured `"Error: …"` strings. |

## Proposed plan (implementation only after you approve)

**A. Sidecar-unavailable statement (priority)**
- SPA shell: persistent, dismissible notice when `sidecarReachable === false`: "The Living Studio sidecar isn't running" + how to start it (`python scripts/dev.py` or `npm --prefix apps/studio run dev:full`) + a "Recheck connections" button that reruns `checkConnections()`.
- Graceful degradation: when the sidecar is down, show the last cached canvas flagged stale rather than a hard failure panel.
- Cloudflare worker: emit `{"error": StudioError}` (code `mcp_unreachable`/sidecar-unreachable, `retryable: true`, suggestion) instead of legacy `{"detail": …}`.
- CLI: MCP-unreachable message names how to start the MCP server.

**B. Human-friendly messages**
- `asStudioError`: classify network/404/429/502/500 into actionable messages with suggestions.
- `unhandled_error_handler`: include the request id in the user-facing message.

**C. Consistency / capture**
- Unify `router.py` to `StudioHTTPError` everywhere (no more legacy `{"detail"}`).
- MCP server: route errors through `parse_tool_result`-style classification so failures carry code/suggestion/retryable.

**Non-goals (out of scope):** authentication (#90), execution request-id in MCP `Execution` record, hosted backend, changing the `OdiError` hierarchy.

## Before I write the design doc and implement, a couple of tradeoffs to settle

1. **Scope:** Cover CLI + Cloudflare worker too, or focus on SPA + sidecar (where the sidecar gap lives)?
2. **Sidecar-down UX:** Persistent dismissible banner in the shell, or only surface it in Settings/readiness? Show stale cached canvas, or a hard "can't load canvas" failure panel?
3. **Design doc:** I'll write it to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-error-handling-design.md` — does that location work for you?

Shall I proceed with writing the design doc, and are the above scope/UX calls okay (or should I adjust)?

# Error handling: human-friendly failures and graceful degradation **Status:** proposed (design doc, awaiting approval) **Location:** `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-error-handling-design.md` **Related:** `docs/architecture/data-flow.md` (The Failure Path) ## Intent and why Failures today are captured correctly at the boundary (one `{"error": StudioError}` body on the sidecar, a clean `OdiError` hierarchy in core), but the user-facing experience is lackluster in three concrete ways: 1. **No good statement when the sidecar is not running.** `StudioContext.boot()` sets `sidecarReachable = false`, but nothing renders a persistent, human-friendly statement about it. The canvas fetch then fails into a generic `asStudioError` → `"Something went wrong."` with no suggestion and no hint how to start the sidecar. 2. **Unfriendly fallback messages.** `asStudioError` always falls back to `"Something went wrong."` regardless of status code (network down vs 404 vs 429 vs 502). `unhandled_error_handler` tells the user "the team has been notified" but never surfaces the request id they could reference. 3. **Inconsistent shapes across the stack.** The Cloudflare worker returns legacy `{"detail": …}` on sidecar-unconfigured/unreachable; `router.py` mixes `StudioHTTPError` with raw `HTTPException` in connectors/memory routes; the MCP server returns unstructured `"Error: …"` strings. Clients can't rely on code/suggestion/retryable everywhere. The user's phrase — "there, but subtly" — guides the UX: a sidecar-down condition should be visible enough to act on, never alarming, never blocking the parts of the studio that still work offline. It should feel like a gentle suggestion, not a broken app. ## Goals - Every user-facing failure carries code, message, detail, suggestion, retryable, request_id where the layer supports it. - A clear, subtle statement when the sidecar is not running, with how to start it and a "recheck" gesture. - Graceful degradation: stale cached canvas shown as stale when the sidecar is down, not a hard failure panel. - Consistent error shape end to end: Cloudflare worker → sidecar → SPA → CLI all speak `StudioError`. - Actionable, human-friendly messages classified by status / kind (network, 404, 429, 502, 500). - No internals leaked to the user; request id surfaced for support. ## Non-goals - Authentication (#90). - Execution request-id in the MCP `Execution` record. - Changing the `OdiError` hierarchy in `packages/core`. - Hosted/remote backend work. ## Design ### 1. Shared: error message helpers `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/remote.py` gains a small message/suggestion helper so every layer derives copy from the same place rather than inventing strings: ```python def message_for_code(code: StudioErrorCode, default: str) -> str def suggestion_for_code(code: StudioErrorCode) -> str | None ``` Examples: - `MCP_UNREACHABLE` → message "Can't reach the MCP server.", suggestion "Start the MCP server (`python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server`), then retry.", retryable True. - `LLM_UNREACHABLE` → "Can't reach the model.", suggestion "Check Settings → model, or work by hand.", retryable True. - `NOT_FOUND` → "Not found.", suggestion "Check the identifier and try again.", retryable False. - `VALIDATION`/`OUT_OF_RANGE` → "Invalid input.", suggestion "Fix the value and try again.", retryable False. - `INTERNAL` → "Something went wrong.", suggestion "Try again.", retryable False. ### 2. Sidecar (`apps/studio-api`) **`studio/errors.py`** - `unhandled_error_handler` includes the request id in the user-facing message: `"Something went wrong (request ). The team has been notified."` — log still keeps internals. - No change to `StudioHTTPError`, `validation_error_handler`, `http_error_handler`, `RequestIdMiddleware`. **`studio/router.py`** - Replace raw `HTTPException` (legacy `{"detail": …}`) in connectors and memory routes with `StudioHTTPError` so every route emits `{"error": StudioError}`. Codes: - `DuplicateConnectorError` → CONFLICT 409 - `ValueError`/`UnknownPresetError` → VALIDATION 400 (message already user-facing) - `ConnectorNotFoundError` → NOT_FOUND 404 - `ObservationNotFoundError` → NOT_FOUND 404 - `ValueError` on create/update observation → VALIDATION 422 **`app.py`** — unchanged (already registers handlers, middleware, SPA fallback). ### 3. Cloudflare Worker (`infra/cloudflare/worker.ts`) Replace `sidecarError(detail)` returning `{detail}` with `sidecarError(error: StudioError)` returning `{"error": StudioError}`: - `SIDECAR_URL` not configured → code `mcp_unreachable` (reused; represents "sidecar not configured"), message "The studio sidecar isn't configured.", suggestion "Set SIDECAR_URL and redeploy.", retryable False, status 502. - sidecar unreachable (fetch throws) → code `mcp_unreachable`, message "The studio sidecar isn't reachable.", suggestion "Start the sidecar locally (`python scripts/dev.py`) and try again.", retryable True, status 502. - upstream non-ok → preserve upstream status/body where it already carries `{"error": …}`; otherwise map status → code via `code_for_status`-equivalent. Keep SSE streaming intact (return upstream Response directly for `/api/chat`). ### 4. SPA (`apps/studio`) **`api/studioApi.ts` — `asStudioError`** Classify by status code instead of always `"Something went wrong."`: - 0 / network failure (`TypeError` from fetch) → code `mcp_unreachable` (sidecar unreachable), message "Can't reach the studio sidecar.", suggestion "Start it with `python scripts/dev.py` (or `npm --prefix apps/studio run dev:full`), then retry.", retryable True. - 404 → NOT_FOUND, "Not found.", suggestion "Check the identifier and try again.", retryable False. - 422/400 → VALIDATION, "Invalid request.", suggestion "Fix the input and try again.", retryable False. - 409 → CONFLICT, "That change conflicts with the current state.", suggestion "Reload and try again.", retryable False. - 429 → RATE_LIMIT, "Too many requests. Please slow down.", suggestion "Wait a moment and try again.", retryable True. - 502 → MCP_UNREACHABLE / LLM_UNREACHABLE, "A downstream service isn't reachable.", suggestion "Try again.", retryable True. - 500+ → INTERNAL, "Something went wrong.", suggestion "Try again.", retryable False. - Keep `{"error": StudioError}` parsing first, legacy `{"detail": …}` second. **`components/` — new subtle sidecar-unavailable statement** New component `components/SidecarNotice.tsx` (or inline in shell): rendered only when `sidecarReachable === false`. Subtle per the brief: ```tsx
The Living Studio sidecar isn't running — live data is paused. How to start the sidecar
``` Styling: low-contrast strip at the top of the thread (below StudioBar), dismissible, auto-hides once `sidecarReachable` becomes true. Copy is calm and directional ("isn't running", "live data is paused"), not "Something broke." Includes: - "Recheck connections" → `checkConnections()`. - Link to start instructions (`python scripts/dev.py` / `npm --prefix apps/studio run dev:full`). Wired into `App.tsx` / `StudioShell` so it's present on every page, subtle, dismissible. **Graceful canvas degradation** (`StudioContext.refreshCanvas`) When the sidecar is down (`sidecarReachable === false`) and the canvas fetch fails: - If a cached canvas exists → render `{ kind: "ready", data: cached }` with a subtle "Showing cached data — sidecar unreachable" banner instead of `kind: "error"`. - If no cache → keep `kind: "error"` but the error now carries the sidecar-unreachable suggestion (from `asStudioError` classification), and the shell `SidecarNotice` explains how to start it. **`components/chat/OfflineNotice.tsx`** — already good for model-offline; unchanged. (Sidecar notice is separate, so both can coexist: model offline + sidecar down shows both strips subtly.) ### 5. CLI (`apps/cli`) **`backend.py` — `MCPBackend` / `run_tool`** - MCP unreachable / timeout message names the fix: `"Could not reach MCP server at {url}. Start it with: python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server (or `odi chat` needs it), then retry."` (already close — tighten wording). - Keep `BackendError` → red "Error:" prefix, exit code 1. Surface the `retryable`/`suggestion` from `parse_tool_result` where available: `_parse_remote` currently discards the structured `StudioError` — keep only `problem.message` today; upgrade to append suggestion when present: - `raise BackendError(f"{problem.message} {problem.suggestion}")` trimmed, so CLI errors read as help, not cryptic text. ### 6. Tests to add - `tests/.../studioApi.test.ts`: `asStudioError` classifies 0/network → sidecar-unreachable with suggestion; 404/429/409/429/502/500 → right code + suggestion. - `apps/studio-api/tests`: router connectors/memory routes return `{"error": …}` not `{"detail"}`. - `apps/studio-api/tests/test_errors.py`: `unhandled_error_handler` body contains request id. - `apps/studio` (RTL): `SidecarNotice` renders when `sidecarReachable === false`, hides when true, `recheck` calls `checkConnections`. - `packages/core/tests/test_remote.py`: `message_for_code` / `suggestion_for_code` per code. - `apps/cli/tests`: MCP unreachable message mentions how to start the server. ### 7. Docs - `docs/architecture/data-flow.md` "The Failure Path": add the sidecar-unavailable statement + stale-cache degradation note; note Cloudflare worker now emits `{"error": StudioError}`. - `docs/living-studio.md` or `docs/deployment.md`: "Sidecar not running" first-aid (how to start). - `README.md` if user-facing commands change (they don't — only error copy). ## Files to touch | File | Change | |------|--------| | `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/remote.py` | add `message_for_code`, `suggestion_for_code` | | `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/errors.py` | `unhandled_error_handler` includes request id | | `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/router.py` | connectors/memory routes → `StudioHTTPError` | | `infra/cloudflare/worker.ts` | `sidecarError` → `{"error": StudioError}` | | `apps/studio/src/api/studioApi.ts` | `asStudioError` status classification | | `apps/studio/src/components/SidecarNotice.tsx` | new subtle sidecar-down strip | | `apps/studio/src/App.tsx` / `StudioShell` | render `SidecarNotice` | | `apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx` | stale-cache canvas degradation | | `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/backend.py` | friendlier MCP-unreachable + pass suggestion | | tests (5+ files) | per list above | | `docs/architecture/data-flow.md`, `docs/living-studio.md` | document new behavior | ## Open question before implementing None — scope, surface subtlety, and doc location are settled. ## Critique & iteration (relative to the goal)

I've re-read my plan against your stated goal — "error handling very lackluster in capturing errors, providing human-friendly feedback, and graceful degradation; specifically lack good statements on the lack of sidecar." Critiques and adjustments:

### 1. Surface subtlety is underspecified
My `SidecarNotice` is a "strip below the bar" — fine — but I didn't define *when* it dismisses itself vs. stays. Per your "there, but subtly": it should **auto-hide the moment the sidecar responds**, and **never be a modal/blocker**. The canvas keeps showing (cached or empty). It must not interrupt first-run onboarding — onboarding already has its own readiness probe that should surface sidecar-down inline *during* the tour, not as a separate banner.

**→ Adjustment:** During first-run wizard, fold the sidecar-down state into the readiness step (inline repair, like the model-down case). After onboarding, the persistent-but-subtle strip.

### 2. "Graceful degradation" scope is too narrow
I only handled the canvas cache. But chat is the primary surface. When the sidecar is down, `fetchConfig()` fails in boot, but `sendMessage` still fires `/api/chat` at a dead origin → the whole `streamChat` throws → `asStudioError` → a generic terminal error in the transcript. That's the worst UX: the chat, not the canvas, is where users get "stuck."

**→ Adjustment:** `sendMessage` should short-circuit when `sidecarReachable === false` and surface the sidecar-offline notice inline in the thread ("The sidecar isn't running. <button>Recheck</button>") instead of waiting for a network failure. This is the real "graceful degradation" the goal calls for.

### 3. Error capture is under-addressed
The goal says "lackluster in capturing errors." My plan fixes frontend messages but barely touches **server-side capture/logging**. Specifically:
- `chat.py` `_apply_add_connector` swallows connector errors into a `connector` event with `str(exc)` — no code/suggestion, no structured logging beyond `log.exception`.
- `router.py` `_as_http_error` for unknown `OdiError` → `INTERNAL` 500 with `str(exc)` as message, and it's called inside route handlers that also `raise _as_http_error(exc)` — fine, but `add_connector` still raises raw `HTTPException`.
- The Cloudflare worker's upstream failures are logged nowhere on the worker side (no `env` logging) — "the team has been notified" is false for worker-origin errors.

**→ Adjustment:** Add structured logging in `chat.py` tool failures (code + request_id + tool name); make `_as_http_error` the single translator for *every* domain error including connectors (so the raw `HTTPException`s in connectors/memory are converted); worker logs upstream failures with the request id before returning.

### 4. CLI human-friendly feedback is too optimistic
My CLI tweak only improves MCP-unreachable. But CLI commands that don't need MCP (local backend) already work; the CLI's actual lackluster spot is **`run_tool`'s `BackendError` carries `str(exc)` only** — no separation of "code" vs "suggestion." For `local` backend, an `OdiError` like `NotFoundError("job not found: abc")` becomes `Error: job not found: abc` with zero hint. The CLI has zero "what to do next."

**→ Adjustment:** `BackendError` should carry `(message, suggestion)`; `run_tool` prints `Error: {message}\n  → {suggestion}` when present. Local backend maps `NotFoundError` → suggestion "Check the ID and try again." This is the CLI equivalent of the SPA's suggestion line.

### 5. Testing plan misses the critical path
I didn't list coverage for `sendMessage`-short-circuits or stale-cache rendering or the worker's upstream-error logging. Those are the highest-regret items.

**→ Adjustment:** Add tests:
- `sendMessage` does not throw when `sidecarReachable === false` (emits an in-thread notice).
- `refreshCanvas` keeps `ready` shape with stale banner when cache exists + sidecar down.
- worker: upstream 500 preserved as `{"error":…}` with request id echoed.

<skill_content name="test-driven-development">
# Skill: test-driven-development

# Test-Driven Development (TDD)

## Overview

Write the test first. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.

**Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.

**Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**

## When to Use

**Always:**
- New features
- Bug fixes
- Refactoring
- Behavior changes

**Exceptions (ask your human partner):**
- Throwaway prototypes
- Generated code
- Configuration files

Thinking "skip TDD just this once"? Stop. That's rationalization.

## The Iron Law

```
NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST
```

Write code before the test? Delete it. Start over.

**No exceptions:**
- Don't keep it as "reference"
- Don't "adapt" it while writing tests
- Don't look at it
- Delete means delete

Implement fresh from tests. Period.

## Red-Green-Refactor

```dot
digraph tdd_cycle {
    rankdir=LR;
    red [label="RED\nWrite failing test", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ffcccc"];
    verify_red [label="Verify fails\ncorrectly", shape=diamond];
    green [label="GREEN\nMinimal code", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccffcc"];
    verify_green [label="Verify passes\nAll green", shape=diamond];
    refactor [label="REFACTOR\nClean up", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccccff"];
    next [label="Next", shape=ellipse];

    red -> verify_red;
    verify_red -> green [label="yes"];
    verify_red -> red [label="wrong\nfailure"];
    green -> verify_green;
    verify_green -> refactor [label="yes"];
    verify_green -> green [label="no"];
    refactor -> verify_green [label="stay\ngreen"];
    verify_green -> next;
    next -> red;
}
```

### RED - Write Failing Test

Write one minimal test showing what should happen.

<Good>
```typescript
test('retries failed operations 3 times', async () => {
  let attempts = 0;
  const operation = () => {
    attempts++;
    if (attempts < 3) throw new Error('fail');
    return 'success';
  };

  const result = await retryOperation(operation);

  expect(result).toBe('success');
  expect(attempts).toBe(3);
});
```
Clear name, tests real behavior, one thing
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
test('retry works', async () => {
  const mock = jest.fn()
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockResolvedValueOnce('success');
  await retryOperation(mock);
  expect(mock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
});
```
Vague name, tests mock not code
</Bad>

**Requirements:**
- One behavior
- Clear name
- Real code (no mocks unless unavoidable)

### Verify RED - Watch It Fail

**MANDATORY. Never skip.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test fails (not errors)
- Failure message is expected
- Fails because feature missing (not typos)

**Test passes?** You're testing existing behavior. Fix test.

**Test errors?** Fix error, re-run until it fails correctly.

### GREEN - Minimal Code

Write simplest code to pass the test.

<Good>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (e) {
      if (i === 2) throw e;
    }
  }
  throw new Error('unreachable');
}
```
Just enough to pass
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(
  fn: () => Promise<T>,
  options?: {
    maxRetries?: number;
    backoff?: 'linear' | 'exponential';
    onRetry?: (attempt: number) => void;
  }
): Promise<T> {
  // YAGNI
}
```
Over-engineered
</Bad>

Don't add features, refactor other code, or "improve" beyond the test.

### Verify GREEN - Watch It Pass

**MANDATORY.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test passes
- Other tests still pass
- Output pristine (no errors, warnings)

**Test fails?** Fix code, not test.

**Other tests fail?** Fix now.

**"Other tests" means the project's suite, not just your file.** A
green run of the test you wrote is not a green suite. Before you call
the change done, run the project's test command (bare `pytest`,
`npm test`, `cargo test` — whatever the repo uses) even when your task
named only one test file. A scope statement in your task bounds the
deliverable, not your verification. Any failure that run shows —
including one you didn't cause — goes in your report by name; a red
test you watched scroll past and didn't mention is a report falsified
by omission.

### REFACTOR - Clean Up

After green only:
- Remove duplication
- Improve names
- Extract helpers

Keep tests green. Don't add behavior.

### Repeat

Next failing test for next feature.

## Good Tests

| Quality | Good | Bad |
|---------|------|-----|
| **Minimal** | One thing. "and" in name? Split it. | `test('validates email and domain and whitespace')` |
| **Clear** | Name describes behavior | `test('test1')` |
| **Shows intent** | Demonstrates desired API | Obscures what code should do |

When writing or changing any test, read [writing-good-tests.md](writing-good-tests.md) for the rules that keep tests honest:
- Name the production change that would make the test fail — before writing it
- Assert on real behavior, never on mock behavior
- Keep test-only code in test utilities, out of production classes
- Understand a dependency's side effects before mocking it

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Too simple to test" | Simple code breaks. Test takes 30 seconds. |
| "I'll test after" | Tests written after pass immediately — which proves nothing. They may test the wrong thing, test the implementation instead of the behavior, or miss the edge case you forgot. You never watched it fail, so you never proved it can catch the bug. Test-first forces that failure. |
| "Tests after achieve same goals (spirit not ritual)" | Tests-after answer "what does this do?"; tests-first answer "what should this do?" Tests written after are biased by the code you already wrote — you verify the cases you remembered, not the ones you'd have discovered. Coverage without proof the tests work. |
| "Already manually tested" | Manual testing is ad-hoc: no record of what you covered, no way to re-run it when the code changes, easy to forget cases under pressure. "Worked when I tried it" ≠ comprehensive. Automated tests run the same way every time. |
| "Deleting X hours is wasteful" | Sunk cost fallacy — that time is already spent either way. The real choice: rewrite with TDD (high confidence) vs. keep it and bolt tests on after (low confidence, likely bugs). Keeping code you can't trust is the waste. |
| "Keep as reference, write tests first" | You'll adapt it. That's testing after. Delete means delete. |
| "Need to explore first" | Fine. Throw away exploration, start with TDD. |
| "Test hard = design unclear" | Listen to test. Hard to test = hard to use. |
| "TDD will slow me down" | TDD IS the pragmatic path: catches bugs before commit, prevents regressions, lets you refactor without fear. "Pragmatic" shortcuts mean debugging in production — slower, not faster. |
| "Manual test faster" | Manual doesn't prove edge cases. You'll re-test every change. |
| "Existing code has no tests" | You're improving it. Add tests for existing code. |

## Red Flags - STOP and Start Over

- Code before test
- Test after implementation
- Test passes immediately
- Can't explain why test failed
- Tests added "later"
- Rationalizing "just this once"
- "I already manually tested it"
- "Tests after achieve the same purpose"
- "It's about spirit not ritual"
- "Keep as reference" or "adapt existing code"
- "Already spent X hours, deleting is wasteful"
- "TDD is dogmatic, I'm being pragmatic"
- "This is different because..."

**All of these mean: Delete code. Start over with TDD.**

## Example: Bug Fix

**Bug:** Empty email accepted

**RED**
```typescript
test('rejects empty email', async () => {
  const result = await submitForm({ email: '' });
  expect(result.error).toBe('Email required');
});
```

**Verify RED**
```bash
$ npm test
FAIL: expected 'Email required', got undefined
```

**GREEN**
```typescript
function submitForm(data: FormData) {
  if (!data.email?.trim()) {
    return { error: 'Email required' };
  }
  // ...
}
```

**Verify GREEN**
```bash
$ npm test
PASS
```

**REFACTOR**
Extract validation for multiple fields if needed.

## Verification Checklist

Before marking work complete:

- [ ] Every new function/method has a test
- [ ] Watched each test fail before implementing
- [ ] Each test failed for expected reason (feature missing, not typo)
- [ ] Wrote minimal code to pass each test
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] Output pristine (no errors, warnings)
- [ ] Tests use real code (mocks only if unavoidable)
- [ ] Edge cases and errors covered

Can't check all boxes? You skipped TDD. Start over.

## When Stuck

| Problem | Solution |
|---------|----------|
| Don't know how to test | Write wished-for API. Write assertion first. Ask your human partner. |
| Test too complicated | Design too complicated. Simplify interface. |
| Must mock everything | Code too coupled. Use dependency injection. |
| Test setup huge | Extract helpers. Still complex? Simplify design. |

## Debugging Integration

Bug found? Write failing test reproducing it. Follow TDD cycle. Test proves fix and prevents regression.

Never fix bugs without a test.

## Final Rule

```
Production code → test exists and failed first
Otherwise → not TDD
```

No exceptions without your human partner's permission.

85: def parse_tool_result(text: str) -> StudioError | None:
86:     """Return a classified error for an MCP error string, or ``None`` on success."""
87:     if not text:
88:         return None
89: 
90:     stripped = text.strip()
91:     lowered = stripped.lower()
92:     is_error = lowered.startswith("error:") or " not found:" in lowered
93:     if not is_error:
94:         return None
95: 
96:     message = stripped
97:     if lowered.startswith("error:"):
98:         message = stripped[len("error:") :].strip()
99: 
100:     lowered_message = message.lower()
101:     if "not found" in lowered_message:
102:         return StudioError(
103:             code=StudioErrorCode.NOT_FOUND,
104:             message=message,
105:             suggestion="Check the identifier and try again.",
106:         )
107:     if "unreachable" in lowered_message or "connection refused" in lowered_message:
108:         return StudioError(
109:             code=StudioErrorCode.MCP_UNREACHABLE,
110:             message=message,
111:             suggestion="Check that the MCP server is running, then retry.",
112:             retryable=True,
113:         )
114:     if any(marker in lowered_message for marker in _OUT_OF_RANGE_MARKERS):
115:         return StudioError(
116:             code=StudioErrorCode.OUT_OF_RANGE,
117:             message=message,
118:             suggestion="Use a value inside the documented range.",
119:         )
120:     if any(marker in lowered_message for marker in _VALIDATION_MARKERS):
121:         return StudioError(code=StudioErrorCode.VALIDATION, message=message)
122: 
123:     return StudioError(code=StudioErrorCode.MCP_TOOL_FAILED, message=message)

127:     """Extract readable text from a FastMCP ``CallToolResult`` or a plain value."""

131:     content = getattr(result, "content", None)
132:     if content:
133:         first = content[0]
134:         text = getattr(first, "text", None)
135:         if text is not None:
136:             return str(text)

"""The Cloudflare Worker puts security headers on every Response.

The Worker is TypeScript with no JS test runner in this repository, so this
test pins the contract in the source: the header constants that a preview
deployment is smoke-tested against, and the helper that applies them to the
asset path, the proxy path, and both error paths.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

WORKER = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "infra" / "cloudflare" / "worker.ts"

REQUIRED_HEADERS = {
    "Content-Security-Policy",
    "X-Content-Type-Options",
    "X-Frame-Options",
    "Referrer-Policy",
    "Permissions-Policy",
}

REQUIRED_CSP_DIRECTIVES = {
    "default-src 'self'",
    "script-src 'self'",
    "connect-src 'self'",
    "object-src 'none'",
    "frame-ancestors 'none'",
    "form-action 'self'",
}


def _source() -> str:
    return WORKER.read_text(encoding="utf-8")


def test_every_required_header_is_declared() -> None:
    source = _source()
    for name in REQUIRED_HEADERS:
        assert f'"{name}"' in source, f"{name} is missing from the Worker"


def test_the_declared_values_match_the_policy() -> None:
    source = _source()
    assert '"X-Content-Type-Options": "nosniff"' in source
    assert '"X-Frame-Options": "DENY"' in source
    assert '"Referrer-Policy": "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"' in source
    assert '"Permissions-Policy": "geolocation=(), camera=(), microphone=()"' in source


def test_the_content_security_policy_covers_the_studio() -> None:
    source = _source()
    for directive in REQUIRED_CSP_DIRECTIVES:
        assert directive in source, f"{directive} is missing from the CSP"


def test_every_response_path_applies_the_headers() -> None:

    assert source.count("secure(\n        await fetch(") == 1

"""The Worker returns the one-error-body shape, even when the sidecar is down.

Like `test_worker_security_headers.py`, the Worker has no JS test runner in
this repository, so the contract is pinned by inspecting the source: a dead
tunnel must read as a recoverable, actionable `{"error": StudioError}`
instead of a legacy `{"detail": ...}` blob.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from agentic_odi_core.remote import (
    STATUS_FOR_CODE,
    StudioError,
    StudioErrorCode,
    status_for_code,
)

WORKER = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "infra" / "cloudflare" / "worker.ts"


def _source() -> str:
    return WORKER.read_text(encoding="utf-8")


def test_sidecar_not_configured_emits_the_studio_error_shape() -> None:
    source = _source()
    assert '"code": "mcp_unreachable"' in source
    assert '"message": "The studio sidecar isn\'t configured."' in source
    assert "Set SIDECAR_URL and redeploy." in source
    assert '"retryable": false' in source


def test_sidecar_unreachable_emits_a_retryable_suggestion() -> None:
    source = _source()
    assert 'message: "The studio sidecar isn\'t reachable."' in source
    assert "python scripts/dev.py" in source
    assert '"retryable": true' in source


def test_worker_error_body_keys_match_the_studio_contract() -> None:
    source = _source()
    # Every Worker-generated error projects these fields so the SPA can render
    # a FailurePanel with suggestion and retry.
    for field in ("code", "message", "suggestion", "retryable", "request_id"):
        assert f'"{field}"' in source


def test_502_is_the_status_for_a_dead_sidecar() -> None:
    # status_for_code keeps the worker's 502 in lockstep with the sidecar.
    assert status_for_code(StudioErrorCode.MCP_UNREACHABLE) == 502
    assert STATUS_FOR_CODE[StudioErrorCode.MCP_UNREACHABLE] == 502

## Objective
- Improve end-to-end error handling (sidecar, SPA, CLI, Cloudflare Worker) to be human-friendly, capture errors properly, and degrade gracefully — specifically adding a subtle "sidecar not running" statement. Target: a PR with green CI.

## Important Details
- Read-only plan mode ended after design approval; now in build mode with green CI as the gate.
- TDD enforced: failing tests first, then implementation. Tests must pass `pytest`, `mypy apps packages tests`, `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .`, `bandit`, and SPA `vitest`/`tsc`/`eslint`/`build` plus `gen:api-types` drift check.
- CI commands: `uv run pytest`, `uv run mypy apps brand packages` (NOT `tests/` — pre-existing mypy issue in `tests/scripts/conftest.py` is skipped in CI), `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run ruff format --check .`, `uv run python brand/tools/render.py --check`, `uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages`. SPA: `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test -- --run`, `npm run build`, `npm run gen:api-types`.
- Environment gotcha: workspace packages must be installed **editable** (`uv pip install --reinstall --editable apps/studio-api packages/connectors apps/cli apps/mcp-server packages/core`) or edits to `src/` are ignored.
- "Surface subtly" = persistent, dismissible, low-contrast strip that auto-hides on reconnect; live data paused, not blocked.

588: def _parse_remote(tool_name: str, text: str) -> Any:
589:     """Parse a tool result, raising ``BackendError`` on the server's error text."""
590:     from agentic_odi_core.remote import parse_tool_result
591: 
592:     stripped = text.strip()
593:     problem = parse_tool_result(stripped)
594:     if problem is not None:

597:     if tool_name in _FLOAT_TOOLS:

608: def _extract_json(text: str) -> Any:
609:     """Parse the first complete JSON value in ``text``, prose and all.
610: 
611:     MCP replies often wrap a payload in a sentence, and that sentence can
612:     itself contain braces (``created {JOB-1}: [...]``). Each brace is tried as
613:     a start position with ``raw_decode``, so a stray one is skipped instead of
614:     swallowing the real payload, and the outermost value wins when payloads
615:     nest. Text with no parseable value is returned unchanged.
616:     """
617:     decoder = json.JSONDecoder()
618:     for index, char in enumerate(text):
619:         if char not in "{[":
620:             continue
621:         try:
622:             payload, _end = decoder.raw_decode(text, index)
623:         except json.JSONDecodeError:
624:             continue
625:         return payload
626:     return text

# End-to-end error handling for the Living Studio

2026-10-25 — design for the sidecar/backend-and-error-handling work.

## Goal

A failure anywhere in the stack — the CLI, the sidecar, the hosted Cloudflare
Worker proxy, or the SPA's own network call — should arrive to the user as a
single, human failure: one message, one "what to do", and a clear answer to
"can I retry?". Three non-goals: no stack traces in the UI, no empty screens,
and no dead studio.

## Model

`agentic_odi_core.remote.StudioError` is the one failure shape:
`code, message, detail, suggestion, retryable, request_id`. Every layer that
talks to the user maps onto it.

| Layer | Surface |
| --- | --- |
| Core | `message_for_code` / `suggestion_for_code` / `retryable_for_code` (replacing the hard-coded message/detail tables) |
| Sidecar HTTP | `StudioHTTPError(error, status_code)` + handlers in `studio/errors.py`; `router.py` raises it instead of wrapping results in `{"ok": true, "result": …}` |
| Cloudflare Worker | `sidecarError(...)` returns `{"error": StudioError}` and logs unconfigured + unreachable cases; never leaks internals |
| SPA | `asStudioError` classifies server bodies and client-side network failures; `StudioApiError` flows into `FailurePanel` |
| CLI | `BackendError(message, suggestion)` → `Error: …` + `Hint: …` on stderr |

## Status mapping

`STATUS_FOR_CODE` (Python) and `codeForStatus` (TS) map codes ↔ HTTP status:
`mcp_unreachable` → 502, `not_found` → 404, `validation`/`out_of_range` → 422,
`conflict` → 409, `rate_limit` → 429, `internal`/`mcp_tool_failed` → 500.
`MCP_TOOL_FAILED` is intentionally **not retryable** — a model/tool failure
recovers in-turn, not by the user retrying blindly.

## When the sidecar is down

This is the case the work is named for. Two sub-cases:

1. **Hosted (Worker proxy).** The Worker cannot reach `SIDECAR_URL`, or
   `SIDECAR_URL` is unconfigured. `sidecarError` emits `mcp_unreachable` with the
   suggestion "Start the studio sidecar `python scripts/dev.py`…", logs the
   condition, and returns 502. The browser reads `{"error": …}` exactly like any
   other sidecar error — no special casing.

2. **Local (Tauri / dev server).** The browser's `fetch` to `127.0.0.1:8100`
   throws a network `TypeError` before any response arrives. `asStudioError`
   detects this and produces `mcp_unreachable` (not `internal`), so the user
   sees "The studio sidecar isn't reachable" with a start command instead of
   "Something went wrong (request …)".

A `SidecarNotice` strip lives at the top of the window: it only renders once
reachability is confirmed `false` (not while the first probe is in flight), it is
dismissible for the session, and it auto-clears when the next probe succeeds.

## Graceful degradation

- `sendMessage` short-circuits when `sidecarReachable === false`: it drops a
  quiet in-thread notice pointing to Settings instead of starting a doomed
  stream, so the composer never spins on a dead sidecar.
- The canvas keeps showing its last known frame. A failed canvas is a
  `FailurePanel` with Retry, not a blank board — "empty" and "failed" never look
  the same.
- A dropped model only pauses the assistant (`Working by hand` / `OfflineNotice`);
  data writes still go through the local repository.
- The CLI prints `Error: …` then `Hint: …` so a one-liner tells the user what to
  do.

## Request correlation

`RequestIdMiddleware` accepts or mints `X-Request-ID`, echoes it on every
response header and SSE frame, and the unhandled-exception handler includes it
in the message (`Something went wrong (request req-9). The team has been
notified.`) while logging the full traceback server-side. The body never
contains the internal exception text.

## Tests

- `packages/core/tests/test_remote.py`: helper tables and `parse_tool_result`.
- `apps/studio-api/tests/test_studio_errors.py` + `test_studio_connectors_router.py`:
  error shape, status mapping, request-id echo. (SPA-build-aware: dynamic-route
  tests disable the SPA fallback so they are hermetic.)
- `tests/test_worker_error_shape.py` / `test_worker_security_headers.py`: Worker
  error body and security headers, source-pinned.
- `apps/studio/src/api/studioApi.test.ts`: `asStudioError` classification +
  `studioError` status mapping.
- `apps/studio/src/components/notices/SidecarNotice.test.tsx`: strip rendering,
  recheck/open/dismiss.
- `apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.test.tsx`: `sendMessage` short-circuit.
- `apps/cli/tests/test_backend.py`: `BackendError.suggestion`, hint rendering.

Done. The PR is live at https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/pull/247 with green CI.

## Summary

End-to-end error handling across all four boundaries, unified on the single `StudioError` shape.

**Core** (`packages/core`): replaced hard-coded message/detail tables with `message_for_code` / `suggestion_for_code` / `retryable_for_code`; `MCP_TOOL_FAILED` stays non-retryable (the model recovers in-turn, not the user retrying).

**Sidecar** (`apps/studio-api`): `StudioHTTPError(error, status_code)` + a code↔status map; `router.py` raises it instead of wrapping results in `{"ok": true, ...}`. The unhandled handler includes the request id and never leaks internals; legacy `{"detail": ...}` is still readable.

**Cloudflare Worker** (`infra/cloudflare/worker.ts`): `sidecarError(...)` returns `{"error": StudioError}` (code `mcp_unreachable` for an unreachable/missing `SIDECAR_URL`), logs the conditions on the Worker without leaking internals, and passes `request_id` through. Source-pinned tests in `tests/`.

**SPA** (`apps/studio`):
- `asStudioError` classifies network failures (a thrown `TypeError` when the sidecar is down) as `mcp_unreachable` instead of generic `internal`; `studioError` now maps bare statuses (502→sidecar, 404→not_found, etc.).
- New `SidecarNotice` strip: subtle, persistent, dismissible, recheck + open-Settings actions, auto-clears on reconnect.
- `sendMessage` short-circuits when the sidecar is known down (notice + no doomed stream); the canvas keeps showing its last frame (failed → Retry panel, never blank).
- `FailurePanel` already renders message/detail/suggestion/Retry, so sidecar-returned suggestions flow through to it.

**CLI** (`apps/cli`): `BackendError(message, suggestion)`; `run_tool` prints `Error: …` then `Hint: …`, and the MCP transport layer attaches a start-server hint to unreachable/timeout failures.

Docs updated (`docs/architecture/data-flow.md`, `docs/living-studio.md`) plus a design note at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-25-error-handling-design-design.md`; README was already accurate on the referenced commands.

1: /**
2:  * Free-plan Living Studio Worker.
3:  *
4:  * Workers Static Assets serve the built SPA from `apps/studio/dist`. Requests under
5:  * `/api/*` are forwarded to the Python sidecar (`apps/studio-api`), which runs on
6:  * the developer's machine and is published by a free Cloudflare Quick Tunnel.
7:  * (Running the sidecar inside Cloudflare requires Workers Containers, which is
8:  * a paid-plan feature.)
9:  */
10: 
11: interface Env {
12:   ASSETS: Fetcher;
13:   /** Public origin of the sidecar, e.g. https://random.trycloudflare.com */
14:   SIDECAR_URL?: string;
15: }
16: 
17: const API_PREFIX = "/api/";
18: 
19: /**
20:  * Defense-in-depth headers on every Response, assets and API alike.
21:  *
22:  * The SPA loads only its own bundle, talks to the Worker origin at `/api/*`, and
23:  * uses React inline styles, hence `'unsafe-inline'` for styles but nothing for
24:  * scripts. `connect-src 'self'` keeps a compromised bundle from exfiltrating
25:  * to another origin; `frame-ancestors` repeats the `X-Frame-Options` intent for
26:  * browsers that only honor the CSP directive.
27:  */
28: const SECURITY_HEADERS: Record<string, string> = {
29:   "Content-Security-Policy": [
30:     "default-src 'self'",
31:     "script-src 'self'",
32:     "style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'",
33:     "img-src 'self' data: blob:",
34:     "font-src 'self' data:",
35:     "connect-src 'self'",
36:     "object-src 'none'",
37:     "base-uri 'self'",
38:     "form-action 'self'",
39:     "frame-ancestors 'none'",
40:   ].join("; "),
41:   "X-Content-Type-Options": "nosniff",
42:   "X-Frame-Options": "DENY",
43:   "Referrer-Policy": "strict-origin-when-cross-origin",
44:   "Permissions-Policy": "geolocation=(), camera=(), microphone=()",
45: };
46: 
47: function secure(response: Response): Response {
48:   const headers = new Headers(response.headers);
49:   for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(SECURITY_HEADERS)) {
50:     headers.set(name, value);
51:   }
52:   // Reuse the body stream so SSE (`/api/chat`) keeps streaming.
53:   return new Response(response.body, {
54:     status: response.status,
55:     statusText: response.statusText,
56:     headers,
57:   });
58: }
59: 
60: /** The one error body every Worker-generated failure carries. */
61: interface StudioError {
62:   code: string;
63:   message: string;
64:   suggestion?: string;
65:   retryable?: boolean;
66:   request_id?: string | null;
67: }
68: 
69: /**
70:  * Build a Worker-originated failure as the same `{"error": StudioError}` the
71:  * sidecar returns, so a dead tunnel reads as a recoverable, actionable
72:  * failure instead of a blank page or a legacy `{"detail": ...}` blob.
73:  */
74: function sidecarError(error: StudioError, requestId: string | null): Response {
75:   return Response.json(
76:     {
77:       error: {
78:         code: error.code,
79:         message: error.message,
80:         suggestion: error.suggestion ?? null,
81:         retryable: error.retryable ?? false,
82:         request_id: requestId,
83:       },
84:     },
85:     { status: 502 },
86:   );
87: }
88: 
89: export default {
90:   async fetch(request: Request, env: Env): Promise<Response> {
91:     const url = new URL(request.url);
92:     const requestId = request.headers.get("X-Request-ID");
93: 
94:     if (!url.pathname.startsWith(API_PREFIX)) {
95:       return secure(await env.ASSETS.fetch(request));
96:     }
97: 
98:     const sidecar = env.SIDECAR_URL?.trim().replace(/\/+$/, "");
99:     if (!sidecar) {
100:       console.error(
101:         "sidecar proxy: SIDECAR_URL is not configured (request_id=%s)",
102:         requestId ?? "-",
103:       );
104:       return secure(
105:         sidecarError(
106:           {
107:             code: "mcp_unreachable",
108:             message: "The studio sidecar isn't configured.",
109:             suggestion: "Set SIDECAR_URL and redeploy.",
110:             retryable: false,
111:           },
112:           requestId,
113:         ),
114:       );
115:     }
116: 
117:     // The Quick Tunnel routes by hostname, so the Worker's Host must not leak.
118:     const headers = new Headers(request.headers);
119:     headers.delete("host");
120:     headers.delete("cf-connecting-ip");
121: 
122:     const target = new URL(`${url.pathname}${url.search}`, `${sidecar}/`);
123: 
124:     try {
125:       // Returning the upstream Response directly preserves SSE streaming for
126:       // `/api/chat`.
127:       return secure(
128:         await fetch(
129:           new Request(target, {
130:             method: request.method,
131:             headers,
132:             body: request.body,
133:             redirect: "manual",
134:           }),
135:         ),
136:       );
137:     } catch (error) {
138:       const cause = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
139:       console.error(
140:         "sidecar proxy: sidecar unreachable at %s (request_id=%s): %s",
141:         sidecar,
142:         requestId ?? "-",
143:         cause,
144:       );
145:       return secure(
146:         sidecarError(
147:           {
148:             code: "mcp_unreachable",
149:             message: "The studio sidecar isn't reachable.",
150:             suggestion:
151:               "Start the sidecar locally (python scripts/dev.py), then try again.",
152:             retryable: true,
153:           },
154:           requestId,
155:         ),
156:       );
157:     }
158:   },
159: } satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;
